language.title.description: Heading of the Language section in Settings.

language.intro.text: Homeroom's own screens are in English for now. Apps on Homeroom use this as their default language, and may offer their own override.
language.intro.description: Explanation under the Language heading in Settings: what choosing a language does today.

language.auto.description: First option in the Language list in Settings: follow the language of the phone or browser instead of a fixed choice.

language.saved.description: Status line under the Language list in Settings after the choice was saved. Keep the check mark.

language.saveFailed.description: Status line under the Language list in Settings when the choice could not be saved and the server gave no reason.

language.loadFailed.text: Could not load that language. Try again.
language.loadFailed.description: Status line under the Language list in Settings when the chosen language's text could not be downloaded.

connectors.title.description: Heading of the Connectors section in Settings, where a person connects AI chat products (Claude, ChatGPT, Codex) to Homeroom.

connectors.intro.text: Work on your apps from a Claude or ChatGPT chat, without using your weekly credits.
connectors.intro.description: Explanation under the Connectors heading in Settings: what connecting a chat product is for. Claude and ChatGPT are product names.

connectors.url.label.description: Label of the read-only field in Settings > Connectors that holds the address to paste into the other product. "MCP" is the name of the standard and stays as is; the wording matches the field name in Claude and ChatGPT.

connectors.url.copyAria.description: Accessible name of the Copy button beside the MCP server URL field in Settings > Connectors.

connectors.howItWorks.summary.description: Tappable line under the MCP server URL field in Settings > Connectors: opens a short explanation of what the address is.

connectors.howItWorks.address.text: This is Homeroom’s address for AI apps. MCP is the standard they use to connect.
connectors.howItWorks.address.description: First paragraph of the "How it works" explanation in Settings > Connectors, about the MCP server URL above it. Homeroom is the product name; MCP stays as is.

connectors.howItWorks.paste.text: Paste it into Claude, ChatGPT or another app that supports MCP. That app can then see your Homeroom apps, file requests and open proposals for you.
connectors.howItWorks.paste.description: Second paragraph of the "How it works" explanation in Settings > Connectors. "It" is the MCP server URL. "file requests" and "open proposals" are verbs: the connected app can submit a change request or start a proposal on the person's behalf.

connectors.howItWorks.approve.text: You need no password or key. The app opens a Homeroom page, and you approve it there.
connectors.howItWorks.approve.description: Third paragraph of the "How it works" explanation in Settings > Connectors: how the other app gets permission. "The app" is the AI app being connected.

connectors.chooseApp.description: Small heading in Settings > Connectors above the list of setup guides, one row per AI product (Claude.ai, ChatGPT, Codex, another agent).

connectors.claude.hint.text: 6 steps · also sets up Claude Code
connectors.claude.hint.description: Second line of the Claude.ai row in the list of setup guides in Settings > Connectors: how long the guide is and what else it covers. The guide has exactly six steps. Claude Code is a product name.

connectors.chatgpt.hint.description: Small hint beside the ChatGPT heading of the foldable setup guide in Settings > Connectors: how many steps it has and where they happen (ChatGPT's plugins directory). Keep the middle dot.

connectors.codex.hint.description: Second line of the Codex row in the list of setup guides in Settings > Connectors. The guide has exactly three steps, done in a command-line terminal.

connectors.generic.title.description: Title of the last row in the list of setup guides in Settings > Connectors: instructions for any other AI coding agent that is not Claude, ChatGPT or Codex.

connectors.generic.hint.description: Second line of the "Another agent" row in Settings > Connectors. The guide has exactly four steps. An "MCP client" is any program that can connect to an MCP server.

connectors.guided.ask.description: Button at the top of a setup guide in Settings > Connectors: opens a new chat in that product which talks the person through setup. {{product}} is the product name, Claude or ChatGPT.

connectors.guided.opens.text: Opens a new {{product}} chat with your connector details already filled in.
connectors.guided.opens.description: Note under the "Ask … to guide you" button in Settings > Connectors. {{product}} is the product name, Claude or ChatGPT.

connectors.guided.orSteps.description: Small heading in a setup guide in Settings > Connectors, between the guided-chat button and the written numbered steps.

connectors.claudeCode.heading.description: Small heading inside the Claude.ai setup guide in Settings > Connectors, above two extra topics that only matter to people using the Claude Code product.

connectors.naming.title.description: Title of a row in the Claude.ai setup guide in Settings > Connectors: the connector must be given the name "homeroom". Keep "homeroom" in lower case, untranslated: it is the exact name to type.

connectors.naming.hint.description: Second line of the "Name it homeroom" row in Settings > Connectors: why the name matters. The rules are Claude Code permission rules that Homeroom ships.

connectors.naming.body.text: Name it exactly <0>homeroom</0>. Claude Code builds its permission rules from that name. A different spelling still works, but the read-only allowlist Homeroom ships in every app repo will not match it, and you will keep being asked to approve each call. The allowlist covers <1>Homeroom</1> as well, so the capitalised form is safe. It also still covers <2>usernode</2> and <3>Usernode</3>, the names this connector went by before, so a connector you added earlier keeps working and there is nothing to redo. Anything else needs the rules rewritten, which the field under “Stop the permission prompts” does for you.
connectors.naming.body.description: Body of the "Name it homeroom" row in Settings > Connectors. Explains which connector names the shipped permission rules cover. The quoted “Stop the permission prompts” is the title of the next row (settings:connectors.prompts.title) and must match it. Keep the text inside the numbered tags exactly as written: those are names and commands the reader types or looks for.

connectors.prompts.title.description: Title of a row in the Claude.ai setup guide in Settings > Connectors: how to stop Claude Code asking for approval before every connector call.

connectors.prompts.hint.text: If Claude Code asks before every call
connectors.prompts.hint.description: Second line of the "Stop the permission prompts" row in Settings > Connectors: when this topic applies.

connectors.prompts.intro.text: Claude Code asks you to approve <0>every</0> connector call by default, including read-only ones like <1>whoami</1> and <2>get_app</2>. Which fix applies depends on where you run it.
connectors.prompts.intro.description: First paragraph under "Stop the permission prompts" in Settings > Connectors. Tag 0 is emphasis on "every"; tags 1 and 2 are tool names and stay exactly as written.

connectors.prompts.ownership.text: Homeroom cannot switch this on for you. Permission rules live in a file on your machine or in your app’s repo, and a connector has no way to write either, which is also what stops any other connector you add from granting itself permissions. Copying one of the blocks below is the whole fix, and it is a one-time thing.
connectors.prompts.ownership.description: Second paragraph under "Stop the permission prompts" in Settings > Connectors: only the person can apply the fix, by copying one of the code blocks shown below it.

connectors.prompts.local.title.text: Claude Code on your own machine
connectors.prompts.local.title.description: Heading of the first of three cases under "Stop the permission prompts" in Settings > Connectors: Claude Code running on the person's own computer.

connectors.prompts.local.body.text: Add this to your own <0>~/.claude/settings.json</0>. It is the only one of the three that covers <1>every</1> repo at once, including repos Homeroom never made.
connectors.prompts.local.body.description: Text under "Claude Code on your own machine" in Settings > Connectors, above a block of settings to copy. Tag 0 is a file path and stays exactly as written; tag 1 is emphasis on "every". "The three" are the three cases listed in this section.

connectors.prompts.local.copyAria.text: Copy the allow rules for your personal settings file
connectors.prompts.local.copyAria.description: Accessible name of the Copy button above the first block of permission rules in Settings > Connectors, the one for the settings file on the person's own computer.

connectors.prompts.web.title.description: Heading of the second of three cases under "Stop the permission prompts" in Settings > Connectors: Claude Code running in the browser.

connectors.prompts.web.body.text: A web session gets a fresh container each time, so a settings file on your own machine is not in it and last session’s approvals are gone. What the container does carry is the repo it checks out, so commit the same block as <0>.claude/settings.json</0> in the app repo. Homeroom writes that file into every app repo it creates, imports or forks; repos that already existed before it shipped do not have one, and adding it is an ordinary commit.
connectors.prompts.web.body.description: Text under "Claude Code on the web" in Settings > Connectors, above a block of settings to copy. Tag 0 is a file path and stays exactly as written. "Commit" is the version-control verb.

connectors.prompts.web.copyAria.text: Copy the allow rules to commit in your app repo
connectors.prompts.web.copyAria.description: Accessible name of the Copy button above the second block of permission rules in Settings > Connectors, the one to commit into the app's code repository.

connectors.prompts.web.trust.text: Claude Code may still ask you to trust the workspace once per container before a repo-level file takes effect. Whether that dialog appears in every web session has not been settled. If you are still prompted after committing the file, that is the reason, and the case above is the fix that does not depend on it.
connectors.prompts.web.trust.description: Closing paragraph of the "Claude Code on the web" case in Settings > Connectors, under its block of rules. "The case above" is "Claude Code on your own machine".

connectors.prompts.chat.title.description: Heading of the third of three cases under "Stop the permission prompts" in Settings > Connectors. All three are product names.

connectors.prompts.chat.body.text: Nothing to do. You approve the connector once when you connect it and it does not ask again per call. The two blocks above are Claude Code’s file format and have no effect in those products.
connectors.prompts.chat.body.description: Text under "Claude.ai chat, ChatGPT and Codex" in Settings > Connectors: these products need no permission rules.

connectors.prompts.readsOnly.text: Reads only. Anything that acts on your behalf (filing a request, opening or advancing a proposal) still asks every time, on purpose.
connectors.prompts.readsOnly.description: Paragraph after the three cases under "Stop the permission prompts" in Settings > Connectors: the rules only silence prompts for calls that read data.

connectors.prompts.spelling.label.text: Connector registered under a different name?
connectors.prompts.spelling.label.description: Label of a text field at the end of "Stop the permission prompts" in Settings > Connectors, where the person types the name their connector actually has.

connectors.prompts.spelling.body.text: Check what your tools are called in your session, the middle part of <0>mcp__homeroom__whoami</0>. If it is not <1>homeroom</1>, <2>Homeroom</2>, <3>usernode</3> or <4>Usernode</4>, type it here and both blocks above are rewritten for it.
connectors.prompts.spelling.body.description: Help text between the "Connector registered under a different name?" label and its field in Settings > Connectors. Typing a name rewrites the two blocks of rules above. Keep the text inside the numbered tags exactly as written: those are names and commands the reader types or looks for.

connectors.codex.add.title.description: Step 1 of the Codex setup guide in Settings > Connectors, shown in bold at the start of the step's text. A complete sentence; the server is the Homeroom MCP server.

connectors.codex.add.body.text: From a terminal where Codex is installed, run the command below, or add the config entry below it to <0>~/.codex/config.toml</0> by hand, which is all the command does. Keep the name <1>homeroom</1>: Codex prefixes the tools with the server name you give it, and it is the name the rest of this page assumes.
connectors.codex.add.body.description: Text of step 1 ("Add the server.") of the Codex setup guide in Settings > Connectors. The command and the config entry are shown in two copyable blocks below the steps. Keep the text inside the numbered tags exactly as written: those are names and commands the reader types or looks for.

connectors.codex.signIn.title.description: Step 2 of the Codex setup guide in Settings > Connectors, shown in bold at the start of the step's text. An instruction to the reader.

connectors.codex.signIn.body.text: Run <0>codex mcp login homeroom</0>. Codex opens your browser on Homeroom’s consent page; approve it there and Codex keeps the token itself. There is no client ID or secret to enter. <1>codex mcp list</1> then shows the server, and the tools are there in your next Codex session.
connectors.codex.signIn.body.description: Text of step 2 ("Sign in.") of the Codex setup guide in Settings > Connectors. Tags 0 and 1 are commands to type and stay exactly as written.

connectors.codex.limit.title.description: Step 3 of the Codex setup guide in Settings > Connectors, shown in bold at the start of the step's text: introduces a current limitation.

connectors.codex.limit.body.text: Codex takes that approval on a <0>127.0.0.1</0> callback, and the hosted Homeroom connector accepts sign-in callbacks only on Claude’s and ChatGPT’s own hosts, so on the hosted platform the sign-in is refused with <1>invalid_redirect_uri</1>. It works against a Homeroom you run yourself in local-development mode. A Codex session without the connector can still build a Homeroom work order: it pushes the branch, and the ChatGPT chat that holds the connector submits it.
connectors.codex.limit.body.description: Text of step 3 ("Know the limit today.") of the Codex setup guide in Settings > Connectors: sign-in from Codex is refused on the hosted platform. Tag 0 is a network address and tag 1 an error code; both stay exactly as written. A "work order" is Homeroom's written hand-off for a coding agent.

connectors.codex.terminal.description: Small caption above the first copyable block in the Codex setup guide in Settings > Connectors: says the command below is typed in a command-line terminal. Lower case, like the file name shown above the second block.

connectors.codex.copyCommandAria.text: Copy the Codex command that adds the Homeroom server
connectors.codex.copyCommandAria.description: Accessible name of the Copy button above the terminal command in the Codex setup guide in Settings > Connectors.

connectors.codex.copyConfigAria.text: Copy the Codex config.toml entry for the Homeroom server
connectors.codex.copyConfigAria.description: Accessible name of the Copy button above the config file entry in the Codex setup guide in Settings > Connectors. config.toml is a file name and stays as is.

connectors.generic.transport.title.text: Give it the connector URL as a Streamable HTTP server.
connectors.generic.transport.title.description: Step 1 of the "Another agent" setup guide in Settings > Connectors, shown in bold at the start of the step's text. "It" is the agent being set up; "Streamable HTTP" is the name of an MCP transport and stays as is.

connectors.generic.transport.body.text: That is the URL in the field above: a public HTTPS endpoint ending in <0>/mcp</0> that takes JSON-RPC over POST. There is no SSE or stdio variant, and nothing to run on your own machine.
connectors.generic.transport.body.description: Text of step 1 of the "Another agent" setup guide in Settings > Connectors. Tag 0 is a URL path and stays exactly as written; JSON-RPC, POST, SSE and stdio are technical names.

connectors.generic.oauth.title.description: Step 2 of the "Another agent" setup guide in Settings > Connectors, shown in bold at the start of the step's text. "It" is the agent; OAuth is the sign-in standard.

connectors.generic.oauth.body.text: Auth is OAuth 2.1 with PKCE and dynamic client registration. A client finds the authorization server through <0>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp</0> on the same origin, registers itself as a public client (no client ID or secret to enter), and asks for the scopes <1>usernode:apps:read</1> and <2>usernode:proposals:write</2>. You approve those once on Homeroom’s consent page.
connectors.generic.oauth.body.description: Text of step 2 of the "Another agent" setup guide in Settings > Connectors: how the agent signs in. Tag 0 is a URL path and tags 1 and 2 are permission scope names; all stay exactly as written.

connectors.generic.callback.title.description: Step 3 of the "Another agent" setup guide in Settings > Connectors, shown in bold at the start of the step's text. The callback is the address the agent's sign-in returns to.

connectors.generic.callback.body.text: Homeroom registers a client only if its OAuth callback is on <0>claude.ai</0>, <1>claude.com</1>, <2>chatgpt.com</2> or <3>openai.com</3> (or a host the deployment’s operator has added). A callback on localhost, which command-line clients use, is accepted only by a Homeroom running in local-development mode. A refused registration answers <4>invalid_redirect_uri</4>, and that is a limit on the platform side rather than something to fix in the client.
connectors.generic.callback.body.description: Text of step 3 of the "Another agent" setup guide in Settings > Connectors: which sign-in return addresses Homeroom accepts. Tags 0 to 3 are host names and tag 4 an error code; all stay exactly as written.

connectors.generic.naming.title.text: Name it homeroom and read your tool list.
connectors.generic.naming.title.description: Step 4 of the "Another agent" setup guide in Settings > Connectors, shown in bold at the start of the step's text. Keep "homeroom" in lower case, untranslated: it is the exact name to type.

connectors.generic.naming.body.text: Tools arrive as <0>mcp__homeroom__whoami</0> in most clients, or as <1>mcp__claude_ai_homeroom__whoami</1> where the client namespaces by product. The part between the first and last <2>__</2> is the server name the permission rules are written for; if it is not one of the spellings they cover, type it into the field under Claude.ai → “Stop the permission prompts”. Have the agent call <3>get_connector_guidance</3> first: it returns the connector’s full operating charter.
connectors.generic.naming.body.description: Text of step 4 of the "Another agent" setup guide in Settings > Connectors. The quoted “Stop the permission prompts” is a row title on this page (settings:connectors.prompts.title) and must match it; Claude.ai is the row it sits under. Keep the text inside the numbered tags exactly as written: those are names and commands the reader types or looks for.

connectors.approveNote.text: Whichever you use, approve the connection in the browser page that opens.
connectors.approveNote.description: Note under the list of setup guides in Settings > Connectors: applies to every product in the list.

connectors.connected.description: Small heading in Settings > Connectors above the list of chat products that are already connected to this account.

connectors.list.loading.description: Shown in place of the list of connected chat products in Settings > Connectors while it loads.

connectors.list.empty.description: Shown in place of the list of connected chat products in Settings > Connectors when none is connected.

connectors.list.disconnect.description: Button on a connected chat product's row in Settings > Connectors: removes that product's access to Homeroom.

connectors.claudeSteps.open.title.description: Step 1 of the Claude.ai connector setup steps, shown in Settings > Connectors and on a dev session's hand-off page. Shown in bold at the start of the step's text; an instruction to the reader.

connectors.claudeSteps.open.body.text: Go to <0>Customize → Connectors</0> in Claude (<1>claude.ai/customize/connectors</1>). This is where both directory connectors and your own custom ones live.
connectors.claudeSteps.open.body.description: Text of step 1 of the Claude.ai connector setup steps, shown in Settings > Connectors and on a dev session's hand-off page. Tag 0 is a menu path in Claude's own interface (use Claude's wording in the target language if it differs); tag 1 is a web address and stays exactly as written.

connectors.claudeSteps.start.title.description: Step 2 of the Claude.ai connector setup steps, shown in Settings > Connectors and on a dev session's hand-off page. Shown in bold at the start of the step's text; an instruction to the reader.

connectors.claudeSteps.start.body.text: Click the <0>+</0> button, then choose “Add custom connector”. In the dialog, put <1>homeroom</1> in the Name field, exactly that spelling: Claude Code builds its permission rules from what you type here, and the read-only allowlist Homeroom ships in every app repo matches only the names it knows. On Team or Enterprise plans this option isn’t there for members, so an Owner adds it first from Organization settings → Connectors (Add → hover “Custom” → “Web”).
connectors.claudeSteps.start.body.description: Text of step 2 of the Claude.ai connector setup steps, shown in Settings > Connectors and on a dev session's hand-off page. Tag 0 is the plus sign on a button; tag 1 is the exact name to type and stays "homeroom". The quoted words are labels in Claude's own interface.

connectors.claudeSteps.paste.title.description: Step 3 of the Claude.ai connector setup steps, shown in Settings > Connectors and on a dev session's hand-off page. Shown in bold at the start of the step's text; an instruction to the reader.

connectors.claudeSteps.paste.body.text: For Homeroom that is the MCP server URL above, a public HTTPS endpoint ending in <0>/mcp</0>. A custom server must be reachable from Anthropic’s cloud, not just from your machine.
connectors.claudeSteps.paste.body.description: Text of step 3 of the Claude.ai connector setup steps, shown in Settings > Connectors and on a dev session's hand-off page. "The MCP server URL above" is a field shown above the steps. Tag 0 is a URL ending and stays exactly as written. Anthropic is the company that makes Claude.

connectors.claudeSteps.oauth.title.description: Step 4 of the Claude.ai connector setup steps, shown in Settings > Connectors and on a dev session's hand-off page. Shown in bold at the start of the step's text; an instruction to the reader.

connectors.claudeSteps.oauth.body.text: If a server requires OAuth, open “Advanced settings” and enter your OAuth Client ID and Client Secret. Skip this for Homeroom: it uses dynamic client registration, so there is nothing to enter.
connectors.claudeSteps.oauth.body.description: Text of step 4 of the Claude.ai connector setup steps, shown in Settings > Connectors and on a dev session's hand-off page: this step can be skipped for Homeroom. The quoted words and "Client ID", "Client Secret" are labels in Claude's own interface.

connectors.claudeSteps.save.title.description: Step 5 of the Claude.ai connector setup steps, shown in Settings > Connectors and on a dev session's hand-off page. Shown in bold at the start of the step's text; an instruction to the reader.

connectors.claudeSteps.save.body.text: Click “Add” to finish configuring, then click “Connect” next to the connector. You’ll be redirected through the OAuth flow; review the scopes it asks for before approving.
connectors.claudeSteps.save.body.description: Text of step 5 of the Claude.ai connector setup steps, shown in Settings > Connectors and on a dev session's hand-off page. “Add” and “Connect” are buttons in Claude's own interface. "Scopes" are the permissions the connection asks for.

connectors.claudeSteps.enable.title.description: Step 6 of the Claude.ai connector setup steps, shown in Settings > Connectors and on a dev session's hand-off page. Shown in bold at the start of the step's text. "It" is the connector; a conversation is a chat in Claude.

connectors.claudeSteps.enable.body.text: In a chat, use the <0>+</0> button at the lower left, then “Connectors”, and toggle your connector on. Toggles are per-conversation, so you control which chats can reach it.
connectors.claudeSteps.enable.body.description: Text of step 6 of the Claude.ai connector setup steps, shown in Settings > Connectors and on a dev session's hand-off page. Tag 0 is the plus sign on a button; “Connectors” is a menu item in Claude's own interface.

connectors.chatgptSteps.directory.title.description: Step 1 of the ChatGPT connector setup steps, shown in Settings > Connectors and on a dev session's hand-off page. Shown in bold at the start of the step's text; an instruction to the reader. The plugins directory is a page of ChatGPT.

connectors.chatgptSteps.directory.body.text: Go to <0>chatgpt.com/plugins</0> in your browser. Plugin and MCP setup is currently a web feature.
connectors.chatgptSteps.directory.body.description: Text of step 1 of the ChatGPT connector setup steps, shown in Settings > Connectors and on a dev session's hand-off page. <0></0> is a link to that address; keep the address as it is. MCP is the name of the protocol connectors use.

connectors.chatgptSteps.create.title.description: Step 2 of the ChatGPT connector setup steps, shown in Settings > Connectors and on a dev session's hand-off page. Shown in bold at the start of the step's text; an instruction to the reader. MCP is a protocol name.

connectors.chatgptSteps.create.body.text: Click <0>“Add plugin”</0>, then choose <1>“Create custom MCP server”</1>.
connectors.chatgptSteps.create.body.description: Text of step 2 of the ChatGPT connector setup steps, shown in Settings > Connectors and on a dev session's hand-off page. The two quoted names are buttons in ChatGPT's own interface, drawn in bold; write them as ChatGPT shows them in the reader's language if known, otherwise keep the English.

connectors.chatgptSteps.url.title.description: Step 3 of the ChatGPT connector setup steps, shown in Settings > Connectors and on a dev session's hand-off page. Shown in bold at the start of the step's text; the address to enter is shown right after it. Homeroom is the product's name.

connectors.chatgptSteps.use.title.text: Turn the server on in a chat.
connectors.chatgptSteps.use.title.description: Step 4 of the ChatGPT connector setup steps, shown in Settings > Connectors and on a dev session's hand-off page. Shown in bold at the start of the step's text; an instruction to the reader. The server is the MCP server just created.

connectors.chatgptSteps.use.body.text: Open the <0>+</0> / connector picker next to the message box, select the server you just created, and set it as active. Now ask ChatGPT to perform something that uses one of the tools, for example: <1>“Use my MCP server to list the open support tickets.”</1> When appropriate, ChatGPT will call the tools your MCP server exposes and use their results in the conversation.
connectors.chatgptSteps.use.body.description: Text of step 4 of the ChatGPT connector setup steps, shown in Settings > Connectors and on a dev session's hand-off page. <0></0> holds the plus sign that is on the button; keep it. <1></1> is an example request in italics.

connectors.chatgptSteps.inShort.text: <0>In short:</0> chatgpt.com/plugins → Add plugin → Create custom MCP server → enter the Homeroom MCP server URL → connector picker → set it active.
connectors.chatgptSteps.inShort.description: Summary line under the ChatGPT connector setup steps: the same steps as a chain. <0></0> is the bold lead-in. Keep the arrows and the address; "Add plugin" and "Create custom MCP server" are button names in ChatGPT.

linkedAccounts.title.description: Heading of the Linked accounts section in Settings, where a person connects a GitHub or X account to raise their weekly AI credits.

linkedAccounts.intro.text: We pay for these credits, so a connected account helps us stop one person making many.
linkedAccounts.intro.description: Explanation under the Linked accounts heading in Settings: why connecting a GitHub or X account raises weekly credits. "Making many" means making many Homeroom accounts.

linkedAccounts.scope.text: Homeroom asks for<0> no access to your repositories </0>and stores no provider token. Connecting confirms you control the account. It is not proof of unique humanity.
linkedAccounts.scope.description: Note under the list of linked accounts in Settings: what connecting a GitHub or X account does and does not give Homeroom. Tag 0 is bold. The spaces just inside the tag are the only spaces around those words, so keep one on each side, inside the tag.

linkedAccounts.dailyCredits.description: Small heading above the list in Settings > Linked accounts that shows the person's weekly AI credit level and the accounts that raise it.

linkedAccounts.auditNote.text: Review or revoke this authorization at <0>{{address}}</0>.
linkedAccounts.auditNote.description: Line in an opened GitHub or X row in Settings > Linked accounts. Tag 0 is a link to the provider's own page of authorized apps; {{address}} is that page's web address as text, for example github.com/settings/applications.

linkedAccounts.showOnProfile.description: Label of a switch in an opened GitHub or X row in Settings > Linked accounts: whether the linked account is shown on the person's public Homeroom profile.

linkedAccounts.disconnect.description: Button in an opened GitHub or X row in Settings > Linked accounts: unlinks that account from the Homeroom account.

linkedAccounts.status.openingBrowser.description: Status line under a GitHub or X row in Settings > Linked accounts, in the phone app, while the system browser is being opened to connect the account.

linkedAccounts.status.finishConnecting.text: Finish connecting in your browser, then return to the app. Sign in with the same Homeroom account if asked.
linkedAccounts.status.finishConnecting.description: Status line under a GitHub or X row in Settings > Linked accounts, in the phone app, after the browser opened to connect an account for the first time.

linkedAccounts.status.finishVerification.text: Finish verification in your browser, then return to the app. Sign in with the same Homeroom account if asked.
linkedAccounts.status.finishVerification.description: Status line under a GitHub or X row in Settings > Linked accounts, in the phone app, after the browser opened to re-verify or change an already linked account.

linkedAccounts.status.savingVisibility.description: Status line under a GitHub or X row in Settings > Linked accounts while the "Show on public profile" switch is being saved.

linkedAccounts.status.visibilityFailed.description: Error under a GitHub or X row in Settings > Linked accounts when the "Show on public profile" switch could not be saved and the server gave no reason.

linkedAccounts.status.shownOnProfile.description: Status line under a GitHub or X row in Settings > Linked accounts after the linked account was made visible on the person's public profile.

linkedAccounts.status.hiddenFromProfile.description: Status line under a GitHub or X row in Settings > Linked accounts after the linked account was hidden from the person's public profile.

linkedAccounts.status.replacing.description: Status line under a GitHub or X row in Settings > Linked accounts while the linked account is being swapped for the newly verified one.

linkedAccounts.status.replaceFailed.description: Error under a GitHub or X row in Settings > Linked accounts when swapping the linked account failed and the server gave no reason.

linkedAccounts.status.replaced.description: Status line under a row in Settings > Linked accounts after the linked account was swapped for another. {{provider}} is GitHub or X.

linkedAccounts.status.cancelFailed.description: Error under a GitHub or X row in Settings > Linked accounts when cancelling a pending account swap failed and the server gave no reason.

linkedAccounts.status.replacementCancell.text: No changes made. @{{handle}} is still connected.
linkedAccounts.status.replacementCancell.description: Status line under a GitHub or X row in Settings > Linked accounts after the person cancelled a pending account swap. {{handle}} is the user name of the account that stays linked; keep the @ before it.

linkedAccounts.replacement.aria.description: Accessible name of the confirmation card in Settings > Linked accounts that asks whether to swap the linked account for a newly verified one. {{provider}} is GitHub or X.

linkedAccounts.replacement.title.description: Title of the confirmation card in Settings > Linked accounts that asks whether to swap the linked account for a newly verified one. {{provider}} is GitHub or X.

linkedAccounts.replacement.intro.text: The new account is verified. Nothing changes until you confirm.
linkedAccounts.replacement.intro.description: Text under the title of the account replacement card in Settings > Linked accounts.

linkedAccounts.replacement.current.description: Small caption over the user name of the account that is linked now, on the left of the account replacement card in Settings > Linked accounts. Adjective: the current account.

linkedAccounts.replacement.verified.description: Small caption over the user name of the new account, on the right of the account replacement card in Settings > Linked accounts. Noun: the replacement account, already verified.

linkedAccounts.replacement.showOnProfile.text: Show the replacement on my public profile
linkedAccounts.replacement.showOnProfile.description: Label of a switch on the account replacement card in Settings > Linked accounts: whether the new account will be shown on the person's public profile.

linkedAccounts.replacement.cancelNote.text: Cancelling keeps @{{handle}} connected with its current visibility.
linkedAccounts.replacement.cancelNote.description: Note above the buttons of the account replacement card in Settings > Linked accounts. {{handle}} is the user name of the account linked now; keep the @ before it.

linkedAccounts.replacement.confirm.description: Button on the account replacement card in Settings > Linked accounts: confirms swapping the linked account for the newly verified one.

linkedAccounts.replacement.replacing.description: Label of the "Replace account" button in Settings > Linked accounts while the swap is in progress.

linkedAccounts.diagnostics.summary.description: Tappable line under a row in Settings > Linked accounts, shown only to platform administrators: opens technical details of how sign-in with that provider is configured. {{provider}} is GitHub or X.

linkedAccounts.diagnostics.callbackUri.description: Label before a web address in the administrators-only setup panel in Settings > Linked accounts: the return address that must be registered with the provider. Keep the colon.

linkedAccounts.diagnostics.run.description: Button in the administrators-only setup panel in Settings > Linked accounts: tests whether the provider accepts the platform's credentials. "Run" is a verb.

linkedAccounts.diagnostics.checking.description: Line beside the "Run configuration check" button in Settings > Linked accounts while the check is in progress.

linkedAccounts.diagnostics.accepted.text: {{provider}} accepted the platform’s client credentials. If connecting still fails on {{provider}}’s own page, the callback address above is not registered on the {{provider}} app.
linkedAccounts.diagnostics.accepted.description: Result beside the "Run configuration check" button in Settings > Linked accounts, administrators only, when the check passed. {{provider}} is GitHub or X. "The {{provider}} app" is the developer app registered with that provider.

linkedAccounts.diagnostics.rejected.text: {{provider}} rejected the platform’s client ID or secret. the configured credential pair is wrong.
linkedAccounts.diagnostics.rejected.description: Result beside the "Run configuration check" button in Settings > Linked accounts, administrators only, when the provider refused the credentials. {{provider}} is GitHub or X. The English second sentence starts in lower case; a translation should be written normally.

linkedAccounts.diagnostics.unreachable.text: Couldn’t reach {{provider}} to verify the credentials. Try again shortly.
linkedAccounts.diagnostics.unreachable.description: Result beside the "Run configuration check" button in Settings > Linked accounts, administrators only, when the provider could not be contacted. {{provider}} is GitHub or X.

linkedAccounts.diagnostics.failed.text: The configuration check failed to run. Try again shortly.
linkedAccounts.diagnostics.failed.description: Result beside the "Run configuration check" button in Settings > Linked accounts, administrators only, when the check itself could not be carried out.

linkedAccounts.native.accountUnknown.text: Your account could not be identified. Reopen Settings and try again.
linkedAccounts.native.accountUnknown.description: Error under a GitHub or X row in Settings > Linked accounts, in the phone app, when the app could not tell which Homeroom account is signed in. Settings is the name of the screen.

linkedAccounts.native.updateApp.text: Update the Homeroom app to open account connections in your browser.
linkedAccounts.native.updateApp.description: Error under a GitHub or X row in Settings > Linked accounts, in the phone app, when the installed app is too old to open the browser for connecting an account.

linkedAccounts.native.browserNotOpened.text: Could not open your browser. Tap Connect to try again.
linkedAccounts.native.browserNotOpened.description: Error under a GitHub or X row in Settings > Linked accounts, in the phone app, when the system browser did not open. "Connect" is the button on that row.

cli.title.description: Heading of the section in Settings that lists the credentials approved for command-line tools and coding agents. CLI means command-line interface.

cli.intro.text: Credentials approved for the Homeroom CLI, Codex, Claude Code, or OpenCode. Revoking an active credential takes effect immediately.
cli.intro.description: Explanation under the "CLI & coding-agent access" heading in Settings. Homeroom CLI, Codex, Claude Code and OpenCode are product names.

cli.tokens.loading.description: Shown in place of the list of command-line credentials in Settings > CLI & coding-agent access while it loads.

cli.tokens.empty.description: Shown in place of the list in Settings > CLI & coding-agent access when the account has no command-line credentials.

cli.tokens.revoke.description: Button on a credential's row in Settings > CLI & coding-agent access: cancels that credential so the tool using it loses access.

cli.tokens.loadMore.description: Button under the list of credentials in Settings > CLI & coding-agent access: fetches the next page of credentials.

cli.guide.title.text: Set up a local coding agent
cli.guide.title.description: Title of the setup guide card in Settings > CLI & coding-agent access (also shown on a dev session's own-tools page): how to use a coding agent on one's own computer with Homeroom.

cli.guide.intro.text: Start Codex or Claude Code from a local checkout and ask it to create a proposal.
cli.guide.intro.description: Summary under the title of the local coding agent setup guide. Codex and Claude Code are product names; a "checkout" is a local copy of the code repository; a "proposal" is a change put to the community.

cli.guide.clone.title.description: Title of step 1 of the local coding agent setup guide. "Clone" is the version-control verb: download a copy of the code repository.

cli.guide.clone.body.text: Clone Homeroom and enter the checkout.
cli.guide.clone.body.description: Text of step 1 of the local coding agent setup guide, above the commands to copy: download Homeroom's code and change into its folder.

cli.guide.clone.codeLabel.description: Accessible name of the scrollable block of commands under step 1 of the local coding agent setup guide. Lower case in English.

cli.guide.clone.copyAria.description: Accessible name of the Copy button beside the commands under step 1 of the local coding agent setup guide.

cli.guide.start.title.description: Title of step 2 of the local coding agent setup guide.

cli.guide.start.body.text: Run either Codex or Claude Code from the repository directory.
cli.guide.start.body.description: Text of step 2 of the local coding agent setup guide, above the two commands. "Run" is a verb: start the program.

cli.guide.start.codexLabel.description: Accessible name of the block holding the command that starts Codex, in step 2 of the local coding agent setup guide.

cli.guide.start.codexCopyAria.description: Accessible name of the Copy button beside the command that starts Codex, in step 2 of the local coding agent setup guide.

cli.guide.start.claudeLabel.description: Accessible name of the block holding the command that starts Claude Code, in step 2 of the local coding agent setup guide.

cli.guide.start.claudeCopyAria.description: Accessible name of the Copy button beside the command that starts Claude Code, in step 2 of the local coding agent setup guide.

cli.guide.ask.title.text: Ask it to create a proposal
cli.guide.ask.title.description: Title of step 3 of the local coding agent setup guide. "It" is the coding agent; a proposal is a change put to the community.

cli.guide.ask.promptHelp.text: Replace the placeholders with the app and change you have in mind, then send the prompt.
cli.guide.ask.promptHelp.description: Text of step 3 of the local coding agent setup guide, above an example prompt whose placeholders are in angle brackets.

cli.guide.ask.examplePrompt.text: Create a proposal for <0>app name</0> that <1>describe the change you want</1>.
cli.guide.ask.examplePrompt.description: Example prompt in step 3 of the local coding agent setup guide, which the person copies and sends to their coding agent. The two tagged parts are fill-in placeholders, shown in angle brackets (<app name>): translate the words inside the tags.

cli.guide.ask.promptLabel.description: Accessible name of the block holding the example prompt in step 3 of the local coding agent setup guide. Lower case in English.

cli.guide.ask.promptCopyAria.description: Accessible name of the Copy button beside the example prompt in step 3 of the local coding agent setup guide.

cli.guide.ask.follow.text: Follow the agent’s instructions. It will ask you to authorize access on a Homeroom web page; review and approve the request there, then return to your terminal.
cli.guide.ask.follow.description: Closing text of step 3 of the local coding agent setup guide, under the example prompt. "The request" is the agent's request for access.

cli.guide.copyFailed.description: Shown briefly in place of a Copy button in the local coding agent setup guide when the text could not be copied to the clipboard.

cli.guide.copyFailedToast.text: Couldn’t copy. Select the text and copy it manually
cli.guide.copyFailedToast.description: Brief pop-up message when a Copy button in the local coding agent setup guide could not copy to the clipboard.

localAgents.lastSeen.description: Third line of an attached machine's row in Settings: which coding agent runs there and when it last reported in. {{runtime}} is the agent's name, for example Claude Code; {{when}} is a short relative time or a date, for example "5m ago" or "Mar 3". Keep the dot separator.

localAgents.lastSeenUnknown.description: Third line of an attached machine's row in Settings when it is not known when the machine last reported in. {{runtime}} is the coding agent's name, for example Claude Code. Keep the dot separator.

localAgents.detach.description: Button on an attached machine's row in Settings: releases that machine's link to the person's dev session, so the coding agent on it stops working for the session.

grants.title.description: Heading of the section in Settings that lists the apps the person has allowed to use AI on their budget.

grants.intro.text: Apps you've allowed to use AI on your behalf. Their spend counts against your normal weekly budget, plus the per-app cap you set. Revoking takes effect immediately, and a revoked app can be re-enabled here with its previous cap.
grants.intro.description: Explanation under the "App AI permissions" heading in Settings. A "cap" is the most an app may spend per day.

grants.loadFailed.description: Error shown in place of the list in Settings > App AI permissions when it could not be loaded.

grants.empty.text: No apps have asked to use AI yet.
grants.empty.description: Shown in place of the list in Settings > App AI permissions when no app has ever asked for permission.

grants.revoked.description: Badge on an app's row in Settings > App AI permissions: the person withdrew this app's permission to use AI.

grants.reenableNote.description: Note on a revoked app's row in Settings > App AI permissions, beside the Re-enable button. {{cap}} is an amount in US dollars such as 0.50; the dollar sign before it is part of the text.

grants.reenable.description: Button on a revoked app's row in Settings > App AI permissions: gives the app back its permission to use AI.

grants.spentToday.description: Figure on an app's row in Settings > App AI permissions: what the app has spent today out of its daily cap. {{spent}} and {{cap}} are amounts in US dollars such as 0.12; the dollar signs are part of the text.

grants.capLabel.description: Label directly before a number field on an app's row in Settings > App AI permissions: the most the app may spend per day, in US dollars. The dollar sign reads as the unit of the field that follows.

grants.useOwnKey.text: Use my own key past the weekly budget
grants.useOwnKey.description: Checkbox label on an app's row in Settings > App AI permissions: lets the app keep using AI on the person's own Anthropic API key once the daily budget is used up.

grants.revoke.description: Button on an app's row in Settings > App AI permissions: withdraws that app's permission to use AI on the person's budget.

usage.title.description: Heading of the first part of the "AI usage & models" page in Settings: how much AI allowance is left.

usage.intro.text: How much of your AI allowance is left and, once you add your own key, what it has spent this week.
usage.intro.description: Explanation under the Usage heading in Settings. "Your own key" is the person's own Anthropic API key; "it" is that key.

usage.buildingTime.title.description: Small heading over a card on the "AI usage & models" page in Settings: how much of the Homeroom bot's weekly building time the person has used, and on which requests. "Building time" is the bot's time planning and building people's requests; Homeroom bot is a name and is not translated.

usage.buildingTime.used.text: {{percent}}% of this week's building time used
usage.buildingTime.used.description: First line of the Homeroom bot building time card in Settings. {{percent}} is a whole number from 0 to 100, for example "62".

usage.buildingTime.usedUp.text: You've used this week's building time
usage.buildingTime.usedUp.description: First line of the Homeroom bot building time card in Settings when the person has used all of this week's: the bot starts their requests again when the week resets.

usage.buildingTime.none.text: You haven't used any building time this week
usage.buildingTime.none.description: First line of the Homeroom bot building time card in Settings when the bot has done no work on the person's requests this week.

usage.buildingTime.unlimited.text: Your building time has no weekly limit
usage.buildingTime.unlimited.description: First line of the Homeroom bot building time card in Settings for a person with no weekly limit; the list under it still shows which requests used the most.

usage.buildingTime.resets.description: Line under the bar on the Homeroom bot building time card in Settings saying when this week's building time starts again. "Resets" is a verb; its subject, the building time, is left out. {{day}} is the weekday's full name and {{time}} the time of day, both in the person's own clock and format, for example "Sunday" and "8:00 PM".

usage.buildingTime.percent.description: One request's share of the week's building time, at the end of its row on the Homeroom bot building time card in Settings. {{percent}} is a whole number, for example "31".

usage.buildingTime.underOne.description: A request's share of the week's building time when it is more than nothing but less than one percent, at the end of its row on the Homeroom bot building time card in Settings.

usage.buildingTime.untitled.description: A row's title on the Homeroom bot building time card in Settings when the request's own title is not known. {{number}} is the request's number, for example "42".

usage.buildingTime.askedFor.description: Second line of a row on the Homeroom bot building time card in Settings, for somebody else's request that the person asked the bot to build, which counts toward their own building time. {{app}} is the project's name.

usage.buildingTime.others.description: Last row of the Homeroom bot building time card in Settings: every request past the end of the list, together, with their share at the end.

usage.buildingTime.showAll_one.description: Button under the five largest requests on the Homeroom bot building time card in Settings: shows the rest of the requests that used building time this week. {{count}} is how many requests there are in all, counting the five already shown.

usage.buildingTime.showAll_other.description: Button under the five largest requests on the Homeroom bot building time card in Settings: shows the rest of the requests that used building time this week. {{count}} is how many requests there are in all, counting the five already shown.

usage.buildingTime.explainLimited.text: Each request's share of your week. It counts the bot reading, planning and building your requests, and any you asked it to build for someone else.
usage.buildingTime.explainLimited.description: Small explanation under the Homeroom bot building time card in Settings, for a person with a weekly limit. "Your week" is their week of building time.

usage.buildingTime.explainUnlimited.text: Each request's share of what you used this week. It counts the bot reading, planning and building your requests, and any you asked it to build for someone else.
usage.buildingTime.explainUnlimited.description: Small explanation under the Homeroom bot building time card in Settings, for a person with no weekly limit.

usage.buildingTime.demo.text: Staging demo figures, not real numbers.
usage.buildingTime.demo.description: Small line under the Homeroom bot building time card in Settings, shown only on a test copy of Homeroom: says the figures are made up for testing.

usage.spend.heading.description: Small caption in Settings > Usage above the card that breaks down this week's AI spending. Shown only when the person has saved their own API key.

usage.spend.platform.description: Row label in the "This week's spend" card in Settings > Usage: spending that counted against the allowance Homeroom provides. An amount follows on the same row.

usage.spend.ownKey.description: Row label in the "This week's spend" card in Settings > Usage: spending billed to the person's own API key. An amount follows on the same row.

usage.spend.resetUtc.description: Last row of the "This week's spend" card in Settings > Usage, as it reads before the page has worked out the person's local time: when the weekly figures start again.

apiKey.title.description: Heading of the section in Settings where a person saves their own Anthropic API key. Anthropic is a company name.

apiKey.intro.text: Bring your own Anthropic API key to keep working past the weekly limit. Your platform weekly allowance is used first; once it runs out, your key takes over automatically, even in the middle of a running turn, and usage bills directly to your Anthropic account.
apiKey.intro.description: Explanation under the "Anthropic API key" heading in Settings. A "turn" is one round of the AI agent working on a request.

apiKey.savedKeyLabel.description: Row label in Settings > Anthropic API key, before the masked end of the API key that is saved. Noun: an API key.

apiKey.fieldLabel.description: Screen-reader label of the field in Settings where the person pastes their Anthropic API key.

apiKey.remove.description: Button in Settings > Anthropic API key: deletes the saved API key from the account.

apiKey.safety.text: Encrypted at rest, verified against Anthropic before saving, never shown in full after save. The server decrypts it in memory to call Anthropic on your behalf, so don't paste keys into services you don't trust with that level of access. <0>Set tight spend limits</0> on the key itself for defense in depth.
apiKey.safety.description: Security note under the key field in Settings > Anthropic API key. Tag 0 is a link to the page on Anthropic's site where spend limits are set; the sentence continues after the link.

openrouter.intro.text: Use any compatible model for all chat and coding in an OpenRouter session. These sessions do not use your platform Claude allowance. Your account comes with an included OpenRouter key, so OpenRouter is the default and GLM 5.3 Flash is selected when available, while the complete key-visible model list stays available. Models marked Claude Code in the model list run in Claude Code. Keys are encrypted at rest and injected only for each turn.
openrouter.intro.description: Explanation under the OpenRouter heading in Settings. OpenRouter, Claude, Claude Code and GLM 5.3 Flash are product and model names. "Key-visible" means the models this API key is allowed to see. A "turn" is one round of the AI agent working.

openrouter.included.title.description: Title of the status card in Settings > OpenRouter about the OpenRouter API key that comes with every account.

openrouter.personalKey.label.text: Or use your personal OpenRouter API key
openrouter.personalKey.label.description: Label of the field in Settings > OpenRouter where a person pastes their own OpenRouter API key, as an alternative to the included one.

openrouter.personalKey.testAndSave.description: Button under the personal key field in Settings > OpenRouter: checks the pasted API key with OpenRouter and saves it if it works.

openrouter.personalKey.remove.description: Button under the personal key field in Settings > OpenRouter: deletes the person's own saved OpenRouter API key.

openrouter.model.label.description: Label of the list in Settings > OpenRouter where the person picks which AI model their coding sessions use.

openrouter.model.filterPlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the search field above the model list in Settings > OpenRouter. "Provider" is the company that makes a model.

openrouter.model.filterAria.description: Accessible name of the search field above the model list in Settings > OpenRouter.

openrouter.model.favoritesOff.description: Toggle button above the model list in Settings > OpenRouter, in its off state: pressing it narrows the list to the models the person starred. Keep the outlined star.

openrouter.model.refresh.description: Button above the model list in Settings > OpenRouter: fetches the current list of models from OpenRouter again.

openrouter.model.addFavorite.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the star button beside the model list in Settings > OpenRouter, when the selected model is not starred yet.

openrouter.model.favoritesNote.text: Platform recommendations start starred. Your changes override those defaults on every device. OpenRouter filters this catalog for your key and account policies.
openrouter.model.favoritesNote.description: Note under the model list in Settings > OpenRouter, about the star (favorite) marks. "This catalog" is the list of models.

openrouter.reasoning.label.description: Label of a list in Settings > OpenRouter: how much thinking the chosen AI model should spend before answering.

openrouter.reasoning.default.description: Option in the "Reasoning effort" list in Settings > OpenRouter: let the model use its own default amount of reasoning.

openrouter.reasoning.minimal.description: Option in the "Reasoning effort" list in Settings > OpenRouter: the least reasoning.

openrouter.reasoning.low.description: Option in the "Reasoning effort" list in Settings > OpenRouter: little reasoning.

openrouter.reasoning.medium.description: Option in the "Reasoning effort" list in Settings > OpenRouter: a medium amount of reasoning.

openrouter.reasoning.high.description: Option in the "Reasoning effort" list in Settings > OpenRouter: a lot of reasoning.

openrouter.reasoning.xhigh.description: Option in the "Reasoning effort" list in Settings > OpenRouter: the most reasoning.

openrouter.saveDefault.text: Save as my default coding agent
openrouter.saveDefault.description: Button in Settings > OpenRouter: makes OpenRouter, with the model selected above, the coding agent used for the person's new sessions.

openrouter.useClaudeDefault.text: Use Claude Code as my default instead
openrouter.useClaudeDefault.description: Button in Settings > OpenRouter: switches the person's default coding agent back from OpenRouter to Claude Code.

screen.signOut.description: Red button at the foot of the Settings menu: signs the person out of Homeroom on this device.

screen.loadFailed.text: Settings could not be loaded. Check your connection and try again.
screen.loadFailed.description: Shown in place of the Settings sections when the code for the Settings screen could not be downloaded.

nav.sectionsName.description: Accessible name of the sidebar navigation on the Settings screen, which lists the settings pages.

nav.filter.field.description: Placeholder and accessible name of the search box above the Settings menu: typing filters the list of settings pages.

nav.filter.noMatch.description: Shown under the Settings search box when no settings page matches. {{query}} is what the person typed. Keep the quotation marks around it, in the target language's style.

nav.filter.signOut.description: Search result in the Settings search box, in red, shown when the person typed something like "sign out" or "log out": choosing it signs them out of Homeroom.

accountRows.native.name.description: Accessible name of the group at the foot of the Settings menu that holds the wallet, node and staking rows of the Homeroom mobile app. Node means the blockchain node running on the phone.

accountRows.native.heading.description: Small visible heading over the wallet, node and staking rows at the foot of the Settings menu in the Homeroom mobile app. Node means the blockchain node running on the phone.

profile.title.description: Heading of the Profile section in Settings (noun: the person's own profile).

profile.intro.text: Your name, photo and bio, and whether your public page is on.
profile.intro.description: Explanation under the Profile heading in Settings: what the profile editor it links to contains.

profile.edit.description: Link text at the right of the card showing the person's name and photo in Settings > Profile: opens the profile editor.

signIn.title.description: Heading on the Account page of Settings over three rows: Username, Email & recovery and Password, the things a person signs in with.

account.change.description: Link at the right of the Username, Email & recovery and Password rows in Settings: opens a small form under that row to change it.

account.add.description: Link at the right of the Email & recovery or Password row in Settings, in place of "Change", when the account has no email address or no password yet: opens a small form to add one.

username.title.description: Title of the Username row on the Account page of Settings, the first of the three sign-in rows; the person's current username is shown under it.

username.intro.text: Your @handle is how you sign in and the address of your public builder page.
username.intro.description: Explanation under the Username heading in Settings. "@handle" is the username written with an at sign; keep the @.

username.newPlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the field in Settings > Username where the person types the username they want.

username.passwordPlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the password field in the change-username form in Settings: the person confirms the change with the password they have now.

username.codePrompt.text: Your account has no password, so confirm the change with a code we email to your verified address.
username.codePrompt.description: Note in the change-username form in Settings for an account that signs in with emailed codes and has no password.

username.codePlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the field in the change-username form in Settings where the person types the code emailed to them.

username.sendCode.description: Button beside the code field in the change-username form in Settings: emails a six-digit code that confirms the change.

username.submit.description: Button in the change-username form that opens under the Username row in Settings: saves the new username.

username.rules.text: Letters, numbers and underscores, 3–32 characters, so people can still @mention you. Your old handle is kept reserved for you rather than released, so links and mentions that used it keep pointing at you and nobody else can take it. You can change your username again after 30 days.
username.rules.description: Small print in the change-username form that opens under the Username row in Settings: the rules for a username and what happens to the old one. "Handle" means username; "@mention" is naming someone with an at sign in a message.

email.title.description: Title of the Email & recovery row on the Account page of Settings, under which the linked email address is shown. The address is used to recover the account.

email.intro.text: Link a private email address to help you get back into your account. It does not appear on your public profile.
email.intro.description: Explanation at the top of the form that opens under the Email & recovery row in Settings.

email.loading.description: Shown under the Email & recovery row in Settings while the linked email address is being fetched.

email.requestFailed.description: Error in Settings > Email & recovery when loading or changing the linked email address failed and the server gave no reason.

email.none.description: Shown under the Email & recovery row in Settings, in place of an address, when the account has no email address.

email.rowUnverified.description: Shown under the Email & recovery row in Settings when the linked address has not been confirmed yet. {{email}} is the address.

email.rowFailed.description: Shown under the Email & recovery row in Settings when the linked email address could not be fetched; a Try again link sits beside it.

email.recoveryAllowed.text: Once verified, use this email to sign in or choose “Forgot password?” on the sign-in screen.
email.recoveryAllowed.description: Note in Settings > Email & recovery for ordinary accounts. “Forgot password?” is the name of a link on the sign-in screen; translate it the way that link is translated.

email.recoveryNotAllowed.text: Admin accounts cannot use email sign-in or email password recovery. Keep your password safe.
email.recoveryNotAllowed.description: Note in Settings > Email & recovery shown to platform administrators instead of the note about signing in by email.

email.verifyPrompt.text: Verify {{email}}. Your current email stays linked until this succeeds.
email.verifyPrompt.description: Instruction above the code field in Settings > Email & recovery after a verification code was sent. {{email}} is the new email address being verified.

email.codeLabel.description: Label of the field in Settings > Email & recovery where the person types the six-digit code sent to their email.

email.addressLabel.description: Label of the field in Settings > Email & recovery where the person types the email address to link.

email.passwordLabel.description: Label of the password field in Settings > Email & recovery: the person confirms the change of email with their account password.

email.submit.busy.description: Label of the main button in Settings > Email & recovery while its request is being sent.

email.submit.verify.description: Main button in Settings > Email & recovery once a code was sent: checks the typed code and links the email address.

email.submit.sendCode.description: Main button in Settings > Email & recovery: emails a six-digit code to the address typed above.

email.startOver.text: Change email or request another code
email.startOver.description: Secondary button in Settings > Email & recovery while a code is awaited: goes back to the address field so the person can correct the address or have a new code sent.

email.verifiedNotice.text: Email verified and linked to your account.
email.verifiedNotice.description: Confirmation in Settings > Email & recovery after the typed code was accepted.

email.codeSentNotice.text: Check your inbox for a six-digit code. It expires in 10 minutes.
email.codeSentNotice.description: Confirmation in Settings > Email & recovery after the verification code was emailed.

password.title.description: Title of the change-password form that opens under the Password row in Settings.

password.titleAdd.description: Title of the same form in Settings, in place of "Change password", for an account that has no password yet and signs in with a code sent by email.

password.rowTitle.description: Title of the Password row on the Account page of Settings, the last of the three sign-in rows.

password.stateSet.description: Shown under the Password row in Settings when the account has a password.

password.stateNotSet.text: Not set. You sign in with an emailed code.
password.stateNotSet.description: Shown under the Password row in Settings when the account has no password and signs in with a code sent by email.

password.intro.text: Set a new password for web login. If an admin gave you a temporary password, enter it as your current password here. No password yet? Choose one here; until then you sign in with an emailed code.
password.intro.description: Explanation at the top of the change-password form in Settings. The last sentence is for an account that has no password yet and signs in with a code sent by email.

password.currentPlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the first field in Settings > Change password: the password the person has now.

password.newPlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the second field in Settings > Change password: the new password, with its minimum length.

password.confirmPlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the third field in Settings > Change password: the new password typed a second time.

password.submit.description: Button in Settings > Change password: saves the new password, checked against the current one.

password.submitAdd.description: Button in Settings > Add a password, in place of "Change password", for an account that has no password yet: saves its first password.

password.submitWithWallet.description: Button in Settings > Change password in the Homeroom mobile app when the person has no current password: signs the request with their wallet (a cryptographic signature, not signing in) and sets the new password.

password.useWallet.text: Don’t have a password? Create one
password.useWallet.description: Link under the Change password button in the Homeroom mobile app: switches the form to creating a password confirmed by the wallet instead of by a current password.

password.usePassword.description: Link under the button in Settings > Change password in the Homeroom mobile app: switches the form back to confirming with the current password instead of the wallet.

deleteAccount.title.description: Heading of the section at the end of the Account page in Settings where the person deletes their Homeroom account.

deleteAccount.intro.text: Anonymise your account and remove your sign-in access. Shared messages and contributions stay under an anonymous “deleted-user” name.
deleteAccount.intro.description: Explanation under the Delete account heading in Settings. “deleted-user” is the literal name shown in place of the person's; keep it as written.

deleteAccount.open.description: Red button with a warning icon in Settings > Delete account: opens the confirmation form. Nothing is deleted yet; keep the ellipsis.

deleteAccount.formName.description: Accessible name of the confirmation form in Settings > Delete account.

deleteAccount.question.description: Heading of the confirmation form in Settings > Delete account.

deleteAccount.deleted.description: Heading that replaces the question in Settings > Delete account once the account has been deleted, while the device is being signed out.

deleteAccount.whatIsRemoved.text: Your account is anonymised, not erased: your name, email, profile, sign-in access and private account data are removed, and you will be signed out on all devices. This cannot be undone.
deleteAccount.whatIsRemoved.description: First paragraph of the confirmation form in Settings > Delete account: what deleting removes.

deleteAccount.whatStays.text: Messages, votes, shared attachments and public contributions stay available to other participants under an anonymous “deleted-user” name. Their contents are kept, including any personal information you shared in them.
deleteAccount.whatStays.description: Second paragraph of the confirmation form in Settings > Delete account: what other people keep seeing. “deleted-user” is the literal name shown; keep it as written.

deleteAccount.retention.text: Necessary financial and moderation records are retained without your account link. External cleanup may take longer. Copies in backups, other apps, GitHub or the blockchain follow their own retention rules.
deleteAccount.retention.description: Third paragraph of the confirmation form in Settings > Delete account: records that are kept and copies outside Homeroom.

deleteAccount.loading.description: Shown in the confirmation form in Settings > Delete account while Homeroom checks whether this account must confirm with a password.

deleteAccount.loadFailed.description: Error in the confirmation form in Settings > Delete account when that check failed and the server gave no reason.

deleteAccount.connectionError.text: Check your connection and try again.
deleteAccount.connectionError.description: Error in the confirmation form in Settings > Delete account when a request failed without any message, usually because the device is offline.

deleteAccount.passwordLabel.description: Label of the password field in the confirmation form in Settings > Delete account.

deleteAccount.recentSignIn.text: For security, sign out and sign in again if you signed in more than 10 minutes ago.
deleteAccount.recentSignIn.description: Shown in the confirmation form in Settings > Delete account, instead of a password field, to people whose account has no password.

deleteAccount.confirmLabel.description: Label of the field in Settings > Delete account where the person must type a fixed word before the delete button works. {{word}} is that word, DELETE, which is always typed in English capitals.

deleteAccount.submit.description: Red button in the confirmation form in Settings > Delete account: deletes the account. It cannot be undone.

deleteAccount.submitting.description: Label of the red button in Settings > Delete account while the account is being deleted.

deleteAccount.failed.description: Error in Settings > Delete account when the server refused to delete the account and gave no reason.

deleteAccount.signOutFailed.text: Your account is deleted. Retry signing out to clear this device.
deleteAccount.signOutFailed.description: Error in Settings > Delete account when the account was deleted but this device could not be signed out. The button under it tries again.

deleteAccount.finishSignOut.description: Button in Settings > Delete account shown after the account was deleted: signs this device out, when doing so automatically failed.

wallet.title.description: Heading of the section in Settings where the person links their Homeroom Wallet, the crypto wallet in the Homeroom mobile app. A product name.

wallet.intro.text: Link your on-chain identity. Scan the QR code with the Homeroom mobile app.
wallet.intro.description: Explanation under the Homeroom Wallet heading in Settings. "On-chain identity" is the person's blockchain address.

wallet.link.description: Button in Settings > Homeroom Wallet: shows a QR code to scan with the Homeroom mobile app, which links that wallet to this account.

agentFiles.title.description: Heading of the section in Settings where the person uploads files that the AI coding agent follows when it builds for them.

agentFiles.intro.text: Personal files the coding agent follows on every build or plan run you start, in any app. Markdown or plain text only, up to 10 of each kind, 48 KB per file. Changes apply from your next run.
agentFiles.intro.description: Explanation under the Agent instructions & skills heading in Settings. "Build" and "plan run" are two kinds of work the AI coding agent does (a plan run writes the plan for a change); "run" is a noun. Keep the non-breaking space between 48 and KB.

agentFiles.instructions.heading.description: Subheading in Settings > Agent instructions & skills over the list of instruction files the person uploaded for the coding agent.

agentFiles.instructions.upload.description: Small button beside the Instructions subheading in Settings > Agent instructions & skills: picks an instruction file from the device to upload (verb).

agentFiles.instructions.empty.text: No instruction files yet. Upload a markdown file to guide the coding agent on every build you start.
agentFiles.instructions.empty.description: Shown under the Instructions subheading in Settings > Agent instructions & skills when the person has uploaded none. "Build" is a noun: a piece of work the coding agent does.

agentFiles.skills.heading.description: Subheading in Settings > Agent instructions & skills over the list of skill files: packaged abilities the coding agent can use.

agentFiles.skills.upload.description: Small button beside the Skills subheading in Settings > Agent instructions & skills: picks a skill file from the device to upload (verb).

agentFiles.skills.empty.text: No skills yet. Upload a skill file the agent can use while building for you.
agentFiles.skills.empty.description: Shown under the Skills subheading in Settings > Agent instructions & skills when the person has uploaded none.

agentFiles.form.nameLabel.description: Label of the field in the upload form in Settings > Agent instructions & skills: the name the uploaded file is saved under.

agentFiles.form.descriptionLabel.description: Label of the field in the upload form in Settings > Agent instructions & skills, shown for a skill: one line saying what the skill does.

agentFiles.form.descriptionPlaceholder.text: One line: what this skill does
agentFiles.form.descriptionPlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the Description field in the skill upload form in Settings > Agent instructions & skills.

agentFiles.list.loadFailed.text: Failed to load your agent files.
agentFiles.list.loadFailed.description: Error in Settings > Agent instructions & skills when the lists of uploaded files could not be fetched.

agentFiles.file.size.description: Size shown on a file's row in Settings > Agent instructions & skills. {{size}} is the number of kilobytes.

agentFiles.file.view.description: Link on a file's row in Settings > Agent instructions & skills: expands the row to show the file's contents.

agentFiles.file.hide.description: Link on a file's row in Settings > Agent instructions & skills while its contents are shown: collapses them again.

agentFiles.file.viewName.description: Accessible name of the View link on a file's row in Settings > Agent instructions & skills. {{file}} is the file's name.

agentFiles.file.hideName.description: Accessible name of the Hide link on a file's row in Settings > Agent instructions & skills, which collapses the file's contents. {{file}} is the file's name.

agentFiles.file.delete.description: Red link on a file's row in Settings > Agent instructions & skills: deletes that uploaded file after a confirmation.

agentFiles.file.deleteName.description: Accessible name of the Delete link on a file's row in Settings > Agent instructions & skills. {{file}} is the file's name.

agentFiles.file.loading.description: Shown inside an expanded file row in Settings > Agent instructions & skills while the file's contents are being fetched.

agentFiles.file.emptyContent.description: Shown inside an expanded file row in Settings > Agent instructions & skills when the uploaded file has no contents. Keep the parentheses.

agentFiles.file.loadFailedReason.description: Shown inside an expanded file row in Settings > Agent instructions & skills when the file's contents could not be fetched. {{reason}} is the error sentence from the server or the browser.

agentFiles.file.loadFailed.description: Shown inside an expanded file row in Settings > Agent instructions & skills when the file's contents could not be fetched and the server gave no reason.

globalChat.title.description: Heading of the Global Chat section in Settings. Global Chat is the name of Homeroom's AI assistant chat; the part in the tag is shown smaller and grey and marks the feature as experimental.

globalChat.intro.text: Fast, low-cost AI for navigating and using Homeroom. Development work keeps its own model and reasoning setting.
globalChat.intro.description: Explanation under the Global Chat heading in Settings. "Model" is the AI model; "development work" is building apps with the coding agent.

globalChat.loadFailed.text: Global Chat settings could not be loaded.
globalChat.loadFailed.description: Error in the Global Chat settings when they could not be fetched and no reason was given.

globalChat.modelsLoadFailed.text: Compatible models could not be loaded.
globalChat.modelsLoadFailed.description: Error in the Global Chat settings when the list of AI models for the chosen reasoning effort could not be fetched.

globalChat.chooseModelFirst.description: Error in the Global Chat settings when the person pressed Save with no AI model selected.

globalChat.saving.description: Status line in the Global Chat settings while a change is being saved.

globalChat.saveBusy.description: Label of the "Save Global Chat settings" button while the settings are being saved.
