globalChat.saved.description: Status line in the Global Chat settings after the model, reasoning effort and cap were saved.

globalChat.saveFailed.text: Global Chat settings could not be saved.
globalChat.saveFailed.description: Error in the Global Chat settings when saving failed and no reason was given.

globalChat.enabledNotice.description: Status line in the Global Chat settings after the person switched the feature on.

globalChat.disabledNotice.description: Status line in the Global Chat settings after the person switched the feature off.

globalChat.toggleFailed.text: Global Chat could not be updated.
globalChat.toggleFailed.description: Error in the Global Chat settings when switching the feature on or off failed and no reason was given.

globalChat.enable.label.description: Label of the switch at the top of the Global Chat settings: turns the Global Chat feature on or off for this person.

globalChat.enable.description.text: Show your Global Chat conversations in Messages. Classic remains the default experience.
globalChat.enable.description.description: Explanation under the Enable experimental Global Chat switch. Messages is the name of a tab in Homeroom; Classic is the name of the regular, non-AI mode of that tab.

globalChat.needsKey.text.text: Add or claim an OpenRouter key before choosing a Global Chat model.
globalChat.needsKey.text.description: Shown in the Global Chat settings when the person has no OpenRouter API key yet. OpenRouter is the name of the AI provider; "claim" means taking the free key Homeroom offers.

globalChat.needsKey.open.description: Button under that notice in the Global Chat settings: goes to the OpenRouter section of Settings (verb: open).

globalChat.model.label.description: Label of the list in the Global Chat settings where the person picks which AI model answers in Global Chat.

globalChat.model.optionPriced.description: An entry in the Global Chat model list. {{model}} is the AI model's name and {{price}} its price per million tokens, already written out (for example "$0.10/M avg"). Keep the middle dot.

globalChat.model.optionRecommended.description: An entry in the Global Chat model list for the model Homeroom recommends, when its price is unknown. {{model}} is the AI model's name. Keep the middle dot.

globalChat.model.optionRecommendedPriced.description: An entry in the Global Chat model list for the model Homeroom recommends. {{model}} is the AI model's name and {{price}} its price per million tokens, already written out (for example "$0.10/M avg"). Keep the middle dots.

globalChat.model.priceAverage.description: Price of an AI model in the Global Chat settings. {{price}} is a dollar amount such as $0.10; "/M avg" means the average per million tokens. Keep it as short as this.

globalChat.model.priceInOut.description: Price of an AI model in the Global Chat settings when input and output cost differently. {{input}} and {{output}} are dollar amounts per million tokens going in to and coming out of the model; "/M" means per million. Keep it as short as this.

globalChat.model.selectedPriced.description: Small line under the Global Chat model list. {{modelId}} is the selected AI model's technical identifier and {{price}} its price per million tokens, already written out. Keep the middle dot.

globalChat.model.refresh.description: Button beside the Global Chat model list: fetches the list of available AI models again.

globalChat.effort.label.description: Label of the list in the Global Chat settings where the person picks how much reasoning the AI model does before it answers.

globalChat.effort.low.description: Option in the Reasoning effort list in the Global Chat settings. GLM Flash is the name of an AI model. Keep the middle dot.

globalChat.effort.minimal.description: Option in the Reasoning effort list in the Global Chat settings: the least reasoning, which only some AI models accept. Keep the middle dot.

globalChat.effort.medium.description: Option in the Reasoning effort list in the Global Chat settings: a medium amount of reasoning.

globalChat.effort.high.description: Option in the Reasoning effort list in the Global Chat settings: a high amount of reasoning.

globalChat.effort.xhigh.description: Option in the Reasoning effort list in the Global Chat settings: the highest amount of reasoning.

globalChat.cap.label.text: Monthly Chat cap in USD · optional
globalChat.cap.label.description: Label of the field in the Global Chat settings for the most this person lets Global Chat spend per month, in US dollars. Chat here is short for Global Chat. Keep the middle dot.

globalChat.cap.placeholder.description: Placeholder of the monthly cap field in the Global Chat settings: left empty, Global Chat has no spending limit of its own.

globalChat.usage.thisMonth.description: Label of a row in the Global Chat settings; the amount Global Chat has spent this month is shown at the other end of the row.

globalChat.usage.spentOfCap.description: Value on the "Global Chat this month" row when a monthly cap is set. {{spent}} is the dollar amount spent this month and {{cap}} the dollar amount of the cap.

globalChat.usage.overallRemaining.description: Label of a row in the Global Chat settings; the credit left on the person's whole OpenRouter key is shown at the other end of the row. OpenRouter is the AI provider's name.

globalChat.usage.unavailable.description: Value on the "Overall OpenRouter remaining" row in the Global Chat settings when the remaining credit is not known.

globalChat.save.description: Main button in the Global Chat settings: saves the chosen model, reasoning effort and monthly cap.

globalChat.developmentSettings.description: Secondary button in the Global Chat settings: goes to the OpenRouter section of Settings, which holds the AI settings used for building apps.

globalChat.footnote.text: Classic is always the startup mode. This profile only controls Global Chat; development sessions keep their separate defaults.
globalChat.footnote.description: Small print at the end of the Global Chat settings. Classic is the name of the regular, non-AI mode of Messages; "profile" means this group of Global Chat settings.

experimental.title.description: Heading of the section in Settings that holds switches for features still being tested.

experimental.intro.text: Early features we're still testing. They may change or disappear.
experimental.intro.description: Explanation under the Experimental heading in Settings.

experimental.progressEstimate.label.description: Label of a switch in Settings > Experimental: shows an AI-made guess of how far along the coding agent is.

experimental.progressEstimate.descriptio.text: While the coding agent works, a small AI model skims its progress log about once a minute and guesses how far along it is and roughly how long is left. It's calibrated against how long real runs actually take, but it's still a guess and can be wrong. Adds a tiny per-run cost (billed to your own API key if you've saved one above).
experimental.progressEstimate.descriptio.description: Explanation under the AI progress estimate switch in Settings > Experimental. A "run" is one stretch of work by the coding agent.

experimental.sessionBridge.label.text: Session bridge (run this chat on your computer)
experimental.sessionBridge.label.description: Label of a switch in Settings > Experimental. Session bridge is the feature's name: it lets a coding session on Homeroom do its work on the person's own computer.

experimental.sessionBridge.description.text: Adds <0>Your computer · Homeroom session</0> to the list of places a session can be built. You keep the platform chat exactly as it is, with the same transcript, branch and proposal, but its turns run through the Homeroom CLI on your own machine, on your own Claude plan. It needs the CLI installed and attached, so it stays off until you ask for it.
experimental.sessionBridge.description.description: Explanation under the Session bridge switch in Settings > Experimental. The tagged part is the name of an option in another list, shown in a monospace font; translate it as that option is translated. CLI is the command-line tool; Claude is a product name; a "turn" is one request and answer of the coding agent.

experimental.suggestShortcut.label.description: Label of a switch in Settings > Experimental: with it on, "Suggest an improvement" opens a screenshot of the page to tap or click and comment on, instead of a form. "The page" is whatever screen the person is on.

experimental.suggestShortcut.description.text: Suggest an improvement opens on a screenshot of the page. Tap or click what should change and say what; it's posted as a suggestion with the screenshot and your pin. Add more comments to the same suggestion, or post each on its own. The form is one switch away. On a computer, pressing C opens it too. Saved on this device only.
experimental.suggestShortcut.description.description: Explanation under the "Comment on the page" switch in Settings > Experimental. "Suggest an improvement" is the name of a button elsewhere; translate it as that button is translated. "The form" is the other, written way to suggest an improvement. C is a key on the keyboard; keep it.

experimental.localAgents.title.description: Heading of a block in Settings > Experimental that lists the person's own computers attached to run the coding agent.

experimental.localAgents.intro.text: Machines running <0>{{command}}</0>. While one is attached, that session's plan and coding turns run there on your own Claude subscription instead of on Homeroom. Each turn asks in your terminal before it starts; plan turns are read-only, and after a coding turn Homeroom still opens the pull request, builds the preview and runs the checks. Detaching sends the next turn back to Homeroom.
experimental.localAgents.intro.description: Explanation under the Local coding agent heading in Settings > Experimental. {{command}} is a terminal command, shown in a monospace font inside the tag. A "turn" is one request and answer of the coding agent; a "plan turn" writes the plan for a change and a "coding turn" makes it. Claude is a product name.

theme.title.description: Heading of the section in Settings where the person chooses a light or dark appearance.

theme.intro.text: Light, dark, or follow your device. Applies everywhere on this browser.
theme.intro.description: Explanation under the Theme heading in Settings.

theme.controlName.description: Accessible name of the three-way control in Settings > Theme that switches between the light, dark and system appearance.

theme.mode.light.description: Choice in the theme control in Settings: the light appearance.

theme.mode.dark.description: Choice in the theme control in Settings: the dark appearance.

theme.mode.system.description: Choice in the theme control in Settings: follow the device's own light or dark setting.

theme.railPinned.label.description: Label of a switch in Settings > Theme, on a computer: keeps Homeroom's sidebar visible beside an app that is open.

theme.railPinned.description.text: On, the sidebar stays beside an app you open, and the sidebar button at the top left hides it. Off, an app takes the whole window and has a close button instead.
theme.railPinned.description.description: Explanation under the "Keep sidebar open in apps" switch in Settings. "Off" and "On" are the two positions of that switch.

accessibility.textSize.title.description: Heading of the Text size part of Settings > Accessibility.

accessibility.textSize.intro.text: Makes text bigger everywhere on this browser.
accessibility.textSize.intro.description: Line under the Text size heading in Settings > Accessibility, saying what the control does.

accessibility.textSize.controlName.description: Name of the Text size choice in Settings > Accessibility, announced to a screen reader for the three-way control.

accessibility.textSize.normal.description: Choice in the Text size control in Settings > Accessibility: today's text size.

accessibility.textSize.large.description: Choice in the Text size control in Settings > Accessibility: about one eighth bigger than Normal.

accessibility.textSize.larger.description: Choice in the Text size control in Settings > Accessibility: about a quarter bigger than Normal.

accessibility.contrast.label.description: Label of the High contrast switch in Settings > Accessibility.

accessibility.contrast.description.text: Darker text and clearer lines, in light and dark.
accessibility.contrast.description.description: Explanation under the High contrast switch in Settings > Accessibility.

privacy.whoCanMessage.title.text: Who can message or invite me
privacy.whoCanMessage.title.description: Heading of the first setting on the Settings > Privacy page, and the accessible name of its two choices. It decides who may start a direct message with you or invite you to a group chat or a project.

privacy.whoCanMessage.intro.text: Who can start a new conversation with you, invite you to a group chat or a project, or send you a friend request. Conversations you already have keep working.
privacy.whoCanMessage.intro.description: Explanation under the "Who can message or invite me" heading in Settings > Privacy.

privacy.whoCanMessage.shared.description: First choice under "Who can message or invite me" in Settings > Privacy, and the default: only people who are in one of your projects with you, or your friends, can start a conversation or invite you.

privacy.whoCanMessage.sharedDescription.text: Your friends, and people who made or were invited into a project you're in. Joining a public community doesn't count. Anyone else can still send you an invite link.
privacy.whoCanMessage.sharedDescription.description: Small explanation under the "People in projects I'm in" choice in Settings > Privacy.

privacy.whoCanMessage.anyone.description: Second choice under "Who can message or invite me" in Settings > Privacy: anybody on Homeroom can start a conversation with you or invite you.

privacy.whoCanMessage.anyoneDescription.text: Anybody on Homeroom can message you, invite you or send you a friend request.
privacy.whoCanMessage.anyoneDescription.description: Small explanation under the "Anyone" choice in Settings > Privacy.

privacy.discoverable.label.description: Label of a switch in Settings > Privacy, off by default. When on, people who are not in a project with you can find your username when they search for people.

privacy.discoverable.description.text: When this is off, only your friends and people who made or were invited into a project you're in find your username when they search for someone to message, mention or invite. A link to your profile still works.
privacy.discoverable.description.description: Explanation under the "Let people find my profile" switch in Settings > Privacy.

privacy.loadFailed.text: Couldn't load your privacy settings. Try again in a moment.
privacy.loadFailed.description: Error on the Settings > Privacy page when reading the current settings from the server failed.

privacy.saveFailed.text: Couldn't save that change. Try again in a moment.
privacy.saveFailed.description: Error on the Settings > Privacy page when saving a change failed; the control goes back to what it was.

devConsole.title.description: Heading of the section in Settings about the log panel that shows an app's console output and errors.

devConsole.intro.text: The bug icon in the header opens a slide-up log of console output and errors forwarded from the running app.
devConsole.intro.description: Explanation under the Developer console heading in Settings.

devConsole.alwaysShow.label.description: Label of the switch in Settings > Developer console: keeps the bug icon in the header visible even when the app has logged no error.

devConsole.alwaysShow.description.text: When unchecked (the default), the icon only appears once the current app has logged at least one error.
devConsole.alwaysShow.description.description: Explanation under the "Always show the icon" switch in Settings > Developer console.

adminPreview.title.description: Heading of a section in Settings shown only to platform administrators: lets them see Homeroom the way a regular member does.

adminPreview.intro.text: Hide admin-only UI so the app looks the way it does for a regular user. Useful for spotting UX issues that only affect non-admins.
adminPreview.intro.description: Explanation under the Admin preview heading in Settings.

adminPreview.toggle.label.description: Label of the switch in Settings > Admin preview: hides everything only administrators can see.

adminPreview.toggle.description.text: Purely a client-side display toggle, so your server-side admin privileges are unaffected. The page will reload so the rest of the UI picks up the change.
adminPreview.toggle.description.description: Explanation under the "View as non-admin" switch in Settings > Admin preview.

alerts.title.description: Heading of the section in Settings about being told when an AI coding session finishes.

alerts.intro.text: Get a heads-up when an agent session finishes and is waiting for your reply.
alerts.intro.description: Explanation under the "Agent session sound & alerts" heading in Settings. An agent session is a conversation with the AI coding agent.

alerts.toggle.label.text: Play a sound, and notify me when the app is in the background
alerts.toggle.label.description: Label of the switch in Settings > Agent session sound & alerts.

alerts.toggle.description.text: When you're in the app a soft chime plays. A browser can show notifications while its tab stays open. To receive push notifications with the mobile app backgrounded or closed, enable Activity notifications on your phone and Agent sessions below. The test queues a phone push with a 10-second delay so you can switch away.
alerts.toggle.description.description: Explanation under the switch in Settings > Agent session sound & alerts. "Activity notifications" is the name of a switch in the Homeroom mobile app's settings and "Agent sessions" the name of a switch further down this page; translate them as those are translated.

alerts.test.description: Button in Settings > Agent session sound & alerts: plays the sound and sends a sample notification so the person can check it works.

alerts.push.title.description: Heading of the block in Settings that lists which kinds of activity may send a notification to the person's phone.

alerts.push.intro.text: Choose which Social activity can send a phone notification. Your phone's Activity notifications switch remains the master control for that device.
alerts.push.intro.description: Explanation under the Mobile push categories heading in Settings. Social is a name for this part of the product; "Activity notifications" is the name of a switch in the Homeroom mobile app's settings.

alerts.push.loading.description: Status line under the Mobile push categories switches in Settings while their saved positions are being fetched.

alerts.push.messages.label.description: Name of a phone notification category in Settings > Mobile push categories: chat messages (plural noun).

alerts.push.messages.description.text: Conversation invitations, messages, mentions, replies, and reactions.
alerts.push.messages.description.description: What the Messages category covers, under its name in Settings > Mobile push categories.

alerts.push.builds.label.description: Name of a phone notification category in Settings > Mobile push categories. "Builds" is a plural noun: things Homeroom bot is building for the person.

alerts.push.builds.description.text: What Homeroom bot tells you about something you asked for: when it needs you, is ready to try, stops, or goes live.
alerts.push.builds.description.description: What the "Your builds" category covers, under its name in Settings > Mobile push categories. Homeroom bot is the name of Homeroom's building assistant.

alerts.push.inviteActivity.label.description: Name of a phone notification category in Settings > Mobile push categories: activity on invite links the person shared.

alerts.push.inviteActivity.description.text: When someone opens your invite link, joins through it, or says hi for the first time.
alerts.push.inviteActivity.description.description: What the "Your invites" category covers, under its name in Settings > Mobile push categories.

alerts.push.directInteractions.label.description: Name of a phone notification category in Settings > Mobile push categories: things other people do that are aimed at this person.

alerts.push.directInteractions.descripti.text: Mentions, replies to your messages, and friend requests.

usernode.faq.heading.description: Small heading over the expandable help topics in the "Homeroom app: about & legal" block in Settings.

usernode.faq.about.title.description: Title of an expandable help topic in the Homeroom app pages of Settings: what the network behind the app is.

usernode.faq.about.network.text: Your device is part of a new network. It verifies, executes, and contributes compute directly to the network, passively in the background - with no central servers, no hidden infra. As long as users keep the app running, the network will continue to operate, peer to peer, with no external dependencies.
usernode.faq.about.network.description: First paragraph of the About help topic in the Homeroom app pages of Settings. "Compute" means computing power; "infra" is short for infrastructure.

usernode.faq.about.why.text: We're doing this to enable networks that can be hosted end-to-end by their own communities - both for decentralization, and to enable a natural coordination point around participation, where users who help operate and contribute to systems directly realize the benefits from it.
usernode.faq.about.why.description: Second paragraph of the About help topic in the Homeroom app pages of Settings: why the network is run by its users' devices.

usernode.faq.about.testnet.text: Right now we are in testnet as we validate the core layer: block production, consensus behavior, and network reliability. As these stabilize, we'll build upon the unique features of the platform - its decentralization, zero knowledge proofs, and sybil-resistant identity - to introduce new activities, coordination mechanisms, and tools for self-hosted, sybil-resistant communities.
usernode.faq.about.testnet.description: Third paragraph of the About help topic in the Homeroom app pages of Settings. Testnet is a blockchain's test network; "sybil-resistant" means protected against one person posing as many.

usernode.faq.about.thanks.text: Thanks for helping test at this early stage. The app right now is simple, but as we prove out the core functionality, we hope to make possible a new kind of community-owned network, where users can directly run and benefit from the networks they use.
usernode.faq.about.thanks.description: Last paragraph of the About help topic in the Homeroom app pages of Settings.

usernode.faq.blockProduction.title.description: Title of an expandable help topic in the Homeroom app pages of Settings. Block Production is the app feature that produces blockchain blocks.

usernode.faq.blockProduction.lead.text: This feature automatically wakes your device to produce blockchain blocks when your node wins a slot. Here's how it works:
usernode.faq.blockProduction.lead.description: First paragraph of the "What is Block Production?" help topic in Settings; four numbered steps follow. A slot is a moment at which one node is chosen to produce a block.

usernode.faq.blockProduction.selection.text: 1. VRF Selection: each epoch, the network randomly selects which validators will produce blocks using Verifiable Random Function (VRF).
usernode.faq.blockProduction.selection.description: Step 1 of 4 in the "What is Block Production?" help topic in Settings. Keep the number. VRF and Verifiable Random Function are technical terms; an epoch is a fixed period of the blockchain.

usernode.faq.blockProduction.scheduling.text: 2. Slot Scheduling: when you win slots, the app schedules alarms to wake your device ~1 minute before each slot.
usernode.faq.blockProduction.scheduling.description: Step 2 of 4 in the "What is Block Production?" help topic in Settings. Keep the number; "~1 minute" means about one minute.

usernode.faq.blockProduction.production.text: 3. Block Production: at slot time, the app monitors your node and ensures the block is produced.
usernode.faq.blockProduction.production.description: Step 3 of 4 in the "What is Block Production?" help topic in Settings. Keep the number.

usernode.faq.blockProduction.tracking.text: 4. Success Tracking: results are recorded to track your reliability over time.
usernode.faq.blockProduction.tracking.description: Step 4 of 4 in the "What is Block Production?" help topic in Settings. Keep the number.

usernode.faq.platform.title.description: Title of an expandable help topic in the Homeroom app pages of Settings: how reliably block production works on this kind of phone. "Platform" means Android or iOS.

usernode.faq.platform.androidHow.text: Uses Android's exact alarm system (AlarmManager) to wake your device precisely when needed for block production.
usernode.faq.platform.androidHow.description: First paragraph of the "Platform & Reliability" help topic in Settings on an Android phone. AlarmManager is the name of an Android component; keep it.

usernode.faq.platform.androidModes.text: Reliability by mode: Default (Event-Driven) 90-95%, battery-efficient, wakes only during slot windows. Keep-Alive Mode 100%, persistent service, higher battery (~5-10%/hr).
usernode.faq.platform.androidModes.description: Second paragraph of the "Platform & Reliability" help topic in Settings on an Android phone: the two modes and how often each produces its blocks. "Default (Event-Driven)" and "Keep-Alive Mode" are mode names; "%/hr" is percent of battery per hour.

usernode.faq.platform.iosHow.text: Uses a combination of background tasks and keep-alive mode to wake your device for block production.
usernode.faq.platform.iosHow.description: First paragraph of the "Platform & Reliability" help topic in Settings on an iPhone.

usernode.faq.platform.iosModes.text: Reliability by mode: Keep-Alive Mode 99%, app stays awake in foreground, requires charger. Background Only 40-60%, iOS controls execution, not guaranteed.
usernode.faq.platform.iosModes.description: Second paragraph of the "Platform & Reliability" help topic in Settings on an iPhone: the two modes and how often each produces its blocks. "Keep-Alive Mode" and "Background Only" are mode names.

usernode.faq.platform.device.description: Last line of the "Platform & Reliability" help topic in Settings on an Android phone. {{manufacturer}} is the name of the phone's maker, such as Samsung.

usernode.faq.vrf.title.description: Title of an expandable help topic in the Homeroom app pages of Settings. VRF (Verifiable Random Function) is a technical term; a slot is a moment at which one node is chosen to produce a block.

usernode.faq.vrf.what.text: VRF (Verifiable Random Function) is how the network fairly selects block producers. At the start of each epoch, the network runs VRF calculations to determine which validators will produce blocks in upcoming slots.
usernode.faq.vrf.what.description: First paragraph of the "Understanding VRF & Slots" help topic in Settings.

usernode.faq.vrf.statuses.text: Status meanings. Pending: waiting for epoch transition to start calculations. Calculating: VRF evaluation in progress (takes a few hours). Complete: slot assignments are finalized and scheduled.
usernode.faq.vrf.statuses.description: Second paragraph of the "Understanding VRF & Slots" help topic in Settings: what the three statuses Pending, Calculating and Complete mean.

usernode.faq.vrf.winning.text: When VRF selects your node to produce a block at a specific time, you've "won" that slot. Your responsibility is to have your device awake and connected so the block can be produced.
usernode.faq.vrf.winning.description: Third paragraph of the "Understanding VRF & Slots" help topic in Settings.

usernode.faq.vrf.timing.text: Why timing matters: each slot has a ~5-seconds window. If your device doesn't wake up in time or loses network connectivity, the slot is missed and counted as "failed."
usernode.faq.vrf.timing.description: Last paragraph of the "Understanding VRF & Slots" help topic in Settings. "~5-seconds" means about five seconds.

signOut.signingOut.description: Label of the Sign out button in Settings while the sign-out is in progress.

connectors.copy.urlFailed.text: Could not copy the MCP server URL

connectors.copy.personalRulesFailed.text: Could not copy the allow rules

connectors.copy.codexConfigFailed.text: Could not copy the Codex config entry

alerts.test.queueing.description: Status under the "Send test alert" button in Settings > Notifications while the request is being sent.

alerts.test.countdown.queued_one.text: Alert in {{count}}s. Phone push queued. Background or close the mobile app to check for a notification. Stay here for the chime if sound is enabled.
alerts.test.countdown.queued_one.description: Status under the "Send test alert" button in Settings > Notifications, updated every second while the test counts down, when a push notification was also queued for the phone. {{count}} is the seconds left; "s" abbreviates seconds. "Chime" is the sound Homeroom plays in the open page.

alerts.test.countdown.queued_other.text: Alert in {{count}}s. Phone push queued. Background or close the mobile app to check for a notification. Stay here for the chime if sound is enabled.
alerts.test.countdown.queued_other.description: Status under the "Send test alert" button in Settings > Notifications, updated every second while the test counts down, when a push notification was also queued for the phone. {{count}} is the seconds left; "s" abbreviates seconds. "Chime" is the sound Homeroom plays in the open page.

alerts.test.countdown.preferenceDisabled.text: Alert in {{count}}s. Phone push was not queued. Enable Agent sessions under Mobile push categories and try again. Stay here for the chime if sound is enabled.
alerts.test.countdown.preferenceDisabled.description: Status under the "Send test alert" button in Settings > Notifications, updated every second while the test counts down, when no phone push was sent because the "Agent sessions" category is switched off under "Mobile push categories" on the same page. {{count}} is the seconds left; "s" abbreviates seconds. "Chime" is the sound Homeroom plays in the open page.

alerts.test.countdown.preferenceDisabled.text: Alert in {{count}}s. Phone push was not queued. Enable Agent sessions under Mobile push categories and try again. Stay here for the chime if sound is enabled.
alerts.test.countdown.preferenceDisabled.description: Status under the "Send test alert" button in Settings > Notifications, updated every second while the test counts down, when no phone push was sent because the "Agent sessions" category is switched off under "Mobile push categories" on the same page. {{count}} is the seconds left; "s" abbreviates seconds. "Chime" is the sound Homeroom plays in the open page.

alerts.test.countdown.unavailable_one.text: Alert in {{count}}s. Phone push was not queued. Sign in on your phone and enable Activity notifications and notification permission. Push delivery must also be available on the server. Stay here for the chime if sound is enabled.
alerts.test.countdown.unavailable_one.description: Status under the "Send test alert" button in Settings > Notifications, updated every second while the test counts down, when no phone push could be sent because no phone is registered for it. "Activity notifications" is the name of a switch in the phone app. {{count}} is the seconds left; "s" abbreviates seconds. "Chime" is the sound Homeroom plays in the open page.

alerts.test.countdown.unavailable_other.text: Alert in {{count}}s. Phone push was not queued. Sign in on your phone and enable Activity notifications and notification permission. Push delivery must also be available on the server. Stay here for the chime if sound is enabled.
alerts.test.countdown.unavailable_other.description: Status under the "Send test alert" button in Settings > Notifications, updated every second while the test counts down, when no phone push could be sent because no phone is registered for it. "Activity notifications" is the name of a switch in the phone app. {{count}} is the seconds left; "s" abbreviates seconds. "Chime" is the sound Homeroom plays in the open page.

alerts.test.after.queued.text: The test push is queued for delivery. Check your phone; delivery may take a few more seconds.
alerts.test.after.queued.description: Status under the "Send test alert" button in Settings > Notifications once the countdown ends and a push notification was queued for the phone.

alerts.test.after.preferenceDisabled.text: Phone push was not queued. Enable Agent sessions under Mobile push categories and try again.
alerts.test.after.preferenceDisabled.description: Status under the "Send test alert" button in Settings > Notifications once the countdown ends, when no phone push was sent because the "Agent sessions" category is switched off under "Mobile push categories" on the same page.

alerts.test.after.unavailable.text: Phone push was not queued. Sign in on your phone and enable Activity notifications and notification permission. Push delivery must also be available on the server.
alerts.test.after.unavailable.description: Status under the "Send test alert" button in Settings > Notifications once the countdown ends, when no phone push could be sent because no phone is registered for it. "Activity notifications" is the name of a switch in the phone app.

alerts.test.failed.text: Could not queue the test push. Please try again.
alerts.test.failed.description: Error under the "Send test alert" button in Settings > Notifications when the request failed and the server gave no reason.

screen.title.description: Title of the Settings screen in the header (noun: the place where preferences live).

localAgents.demoData.text: Demo data: changes are not saved.
localAgents.demoData.description: Note under the list of attached machines in Settings when the rows are sample data on a preview server.

localAgents.unknownApp.description: Stands in for the app's name in the line under an attached machine in Settings > Connectors & CLI, when the app is unknown. Lower case: it is shown alone or before a session title.

localAgents.unnamedMachine.description: Title of a row in the list of attached machines (computers running a coding agent for this account) in Settings, when the machine was given no label.

localAgents.appAndSession.description: Line under an attached machine in Settings: which app and which coding session it is attached to. {{app}} is the app's name, {{session}} the session's title. Keep the separator dot or use your language's equivalent.

localAgents.detach.confirmNamed.text:
Detach {{machine}}?

Its session's coding turns go back to running on Homeroom. Anything it already committed stays on the branch.
localAgents.detach.confirmNamed.description: Confirmation dialog before detaching a person's own computer from a coding session, in Settings. {{machine}} is the label the person gave the machine. "Detach" is a verb; "branch" is a Git branch. Keep the blank line.

localAgents.detach.confirmUnnamed.text:
Detach this machine?

Its session's coding turns go back to running on Homeroom. Anything it already committed stays on the branch.
localAgents.detach.confirmUnnamed.description: Confirmation dialog before detaching a person's own computer from a coding session, in Settings, when the machine has no label. "Detach" is a verb; "branch" is a Git branch. Keep the blank line.

localAgents.detach.failed.description: Error under the list of attached machines in Settings when detaching one failed.

connectors.setupPrompt.text: I want to add a custom MCP connector. The server URL is {{url}} and it uses dynamic client registration, so there is no client ID or secret to enter. Name it exactly "homeroom". Walk me through it one step at a time and tell me what to click.
connectors.setupPrompt.description: Not shown in Homeroom: a request written in the person's voice, pre-filled into a new Claude or ChatGPT chat by the "set it up" links in Settings > Connectors. {{url}} is the connector address. Keep "homeroom" exactly, in lower case, and keep "MCP".

connectors.load.failed.description: Error in Settings > Connectors when the list of chat apps connected to the account could not be loaded.

connectors.load.invalid.description: Error in Settings > Connectors when the server answered the list of connected chat apps in a form Homeroom could not read.

connectors.hint.notSentYet.text: Homeroom has not sent you this tip in chat yet. It rides along on the first read it answers in a new conversation.
connectors.hint.notSentYet.description: Status line under the "stop the permission prompts" advice in Settings > Connectors, about the tip Homeroom adds to its answers in a chat app (Claude, ChatGPT) telling the person how to stop those prompts. Shown when the tip has never been sent. "Read" is a noun here: a request to read data that Homeroom answers.

connectors.hint.sent_one.text: Homeroom sent you this tip in chat once in the last {{days}} days, most recently {{when}}.
connectors.hint.sent_one.description: Status line under the "stop the permission prompts" advice in Settings > Connectors, about the tip Homeroom adds to its answers in a chat app (Claude, ChatGPT) telling the person how to stop those prompts. How often it was sent. {{count}} is the number of times (1 here), {{days}} the length of the window in days, {{when}} a date and time. {{count}} is available in this form too, although English does not show it: a language whose singular form is also used for 21 or 101 should print the number.

connectors.hint.sent_other.text: Homeroom sent you this tip in chat {{count}} times in the last {{days}} days, most recently {{when}}.
connectors.hint.sent_other.description: Status line under the "stop the permission prompts" advice in Settings > Connectors, about the tip Homeroom adds to its answers in a chat app (Claude, ChatGPT) telling the person how to stop those prompts. How often it was sent. {{count}} is the number of times, {{days}} the length of the window in days, {{when}} a date and time.

connectors.hint.sentWhenUnknown_one.text: Homeroom sent you this tip in chat once in the last {{days}} days, most recently recently.
connectors.hint.sentWhenUnknown_one.description: Status line under the "stop the permission prompts" advice in Settings > Connectors, about the tip Homeroom adds to its answers in a chat app (Claude, ChatGPT) telling the person how to stop those prompts. How often it was sent, when the time of the last one is not known. {{count}} is the number of times (1 here), {{days}} the length of the window in days. The English repeats "recently" by accident of the fallback; write a natural sentence. {{count}} is available in this form too, although English does not show it: a language whose singular form is also used for 21 or 101 should print the number.

connectors.hint.sentWhenUnknown_other.text: Homeroom sent you this tip in chat {{count}} times in the last {{days}} days, most recently recently.
connectors.hint.sentWhenUnknown_other.description: Status line under the "stop the permission prompts" advice in Settings > Connectors, about the tip Homeroom adds to its answers in a chat app (Claude, ChatGPT) telling the person how to stop those prompts. How often it was sent, when the time of the last one is not known. {{count}} is the number of times, {{days}} the length of the window in days. The English repeats "recently" by accident of the fallback; write a natural sentence.

connectors.hint.limitReached.text: That is the limit of {{limit}} per connection per {{days}} days; it will come back once the window rolls over.
connectors.hint.limitReached.description: Status line under the "stop the permission prompts" advice in Settings > Connectors, about the tip Homeroom adds to its answers in a chat app (Claude, ChatGPT) telling the person how to stop those prompts. Follows the sentence saying how often the tip was sent, when it has reached its maximum. {{limit}} is the maximum number of times, {{days}} the length of the window in days. "It" is the tip.

connectors.hint.quietUntilToday.text: It stays quiet for {{minutes}} minutes after each one, so a conversation opened before today at {{time}} will not carry it. One opened after that will.
connectors.hint.quietUntilToday.description: Status line under the "stop the permission prompts" advice in Settings > Connectors, about the tip Homeroom adds to its answers in a chat app (Claude, ChatGPT) telling the person how to stop those prompts. Follows the sentence saying how often the tip was sent, while a pause after the last one is still running and ends today. {{minutes}} is the length of the pause, {{time}} a clock time. "It" is the tip; "one" is a tip, then a conversation.

connectors.hint.quietUntilDate.text: It stays quiet for {{minutes}} minutes after each one, so a conversation opened before {{when}} will not carry it. One opened after that will.
connectors.hint.quietUntilDate.description: Status line under the "stop the permission prompts" advice in Settings > Connectors, about the tip Homeroom adds to its answers in a chat app (Claude, ChatGPT) telling the person how to stop those prompts. Follows the sentence saying how often the tip was sent, while a pause after the last one is still running and ends on another day. {{minutes}} is the length of the pause, {{when}} a date and time. "It" is the tip.

connectors.hint.openNewConversation.text: Open a new conversation to see it again.
connectors.hint.openNewConversation.description: Status line under the "stop the permission prompts" advice in Settings > Connectors, about the tip Homeroom adds to its answers in a chat app (Claude, ChatGPT) telling the person how to stop those prompts. Follows the sentence saying how often the tip was sent, when nothing prevents it from being sent again. "Open" is a verb; "it" is the tip.

connectors.hint.summaryAndAdvice.description: Status line under the "stop the permission prompts" advice in Settings > Connectors, about the tip Homeroom adds to its answers in a chat app (Claude, ChatGPT) telling the person how to stop those prompts. Puts two complete sentences one after the other: {{summary}} says how often the tip was sent, {{advice}} says when it will be sent again. Change only the spacing or order if your language needs it.

connectors.row.connectedUsed.description: Second line of a connected chat app's card in Settings > Connectors: when it was connected and last used. Both parameters are dates with times. Lower case: it is a detail line, not a sentence.

connectors.row.connectedNeverUsed.description: Second line of a connected chat app's card in Settings > Connectors: when it was connected, and that it has not been used yet. {{connected}} is a date with time. Lower case: it is a detail line, not a sentence.

connectors.row.unknownDateUsed.description: Second line of a connected chat app's card in Settings > Connectors: shown when the date it was connected is not known. {{lastUsed}} is a date with time. Lower case: it is a detail line, not a sentence.

connectors.row.unknownDateNeverUsed.description: Second line of a connected chat app's card in Settings > Connectors: shown when the date it was connected is not known and it has not been used yet. Lower case: it is a detail line, not a sentence.

connectors.row.unnamedClient.description: Title of a connected chat app's card in Settings > Connectors when the app gave no name. "Client" is a program connected to Homeroom, not a customer.

connectors.disconnect.failedRetry.description: Error in Settings > Connectors when the server refused to disconnect a chat app from the account.

connectors.disconnect.done.description: Confirmation in Settings > Connectors after a chat app was disconnected from the account.

connectors.disconnect.failed.description: Error in Settings > Connectors when disconnecting a chat app failed and there is no more specific reason.

socialIdentity.load.failed.text: Could not load social accounts. Try again shortly.
socialIdentity.load.failed.description: Error in Settings > Linked accounts. when the list of connected GitHub and X accounts could not be loaded.

socialIdentity.perWeek.description: An amount of AI credits per week, in US dollars, in the weekly-credits list in Settings > Linked accounts. {{amount}} is a number such as 50 or 2.50. Keep the dollar sign.

socialIdentity.tier.unavailable.title.description: Title of the first row of the weekly-credits list in Settings > Linked accounts. when Homeroom could not check how many credits the account has.

socialIdentity.tier.unavailable.note.text: We could not check your credits, so calls we pay for are paused. Your own API key still works.
socialIdentity.tier.unavailable.note.description: Note under the weekly-credits list in Settings > Linked accounts. when the credits could not be checked. "Calls" are requests to an AI model; "we" is Homeroom.

socialIdentity.tier.legacy.title.description: Title of the first row of the weekly-credits list in Settings > Linked accounts. on a server where connecting an account does not change the amount.

socialIdentity.tier.legacy.note.text: Your credits do not depend on a connected account yet.
socialIdentity.tier.legacy.note.description: Note under the weekly-credits list in Settings > Linked accounts. on a server where connecting GitHub or X does not change the weekly AI credits.

socialIdentity.tier.override.title.description: Title of the first row of the weekly-credits list in Settings > Linked accounts. for an account whose amount an administrator set by hand.

socialIdentity.tier.override.note.text: An administrator set this amount. A connected account does not change it.
socialIdentity.tier.override.note.description: Note under the weekly-credits list in Settings > Linked accounts. for an account whose weekly AI credits an administrator set by hand.

socialIdentity.tier.signedIn.title.description: Title of the first row of the weekly-credits list in Settings > Linked accounts. the credits a person gets just for being signed in, before connecting GitHub or X. A state, not an action.

socialIdentity.tier.signedIn.note.text: Either one is enough. Connecting both does not add more.
socialIdentity.tier.signedIn.note.description: Note under the weekly-credits list in Settings > Linked accounts. "Either one" means a GitHub account or an X account; connecting one raises the weekly credits.

socialIdentity.row.reconnectRequired.text: Linked for GitHub attribution. Reconnect once to count it toward weekly credits.
socialIdentity.row.reconnectRequired.description: Amber state text on the GitHub row in Settings > Linked accounts. the account is linked only so code changes are credited to it, and must be connected again before it raises the weekly credits.

socialIdentity.row.noExtraCredits.description: State text on the second connected account's row in Settings > Linked accounts. the first connected account already raised the weekly credits, and this one adds nothing.

socialIdentity.row.notSetUp.text: Not set up on this server.
socialIdentity.row.notSetUp.description: State text on the GitHub or X row in Settings > Linked accounts. when this Homeroom server has no configuration for connecting that provider.

socialIdentity.row.notConnected.description: State text on the GitHub or X row in Settings > Linked accounts. when the person has not connected that account.

socialIdentity.badge.reconnectNeeded.description: Amber badge on the GitHub or X row in Settings > Linked accounts. the account is linked but must be connected again before it counts.

socialIdentity.badge.connected.description: Green badge on the GitHub or X row in Settings > Linked accounts. the account is connected. A state, not an action.

socialIdentity.row.linkedAt.description: Detail on a connected GitHub or X row in Settings > Linked accounts. when the account was connected. {{when}} is a date with time. Lower case: it is a detail, not a sentence.

socialIdentity.row.noTokenGithub.text: Homeroom holds no GitHub access token for your account.
socialIdentity.row.noTokenGithub.description: Reassurance on the GitHub row in Settings > Linked accounts. Homeroom only confirmed who the person is and cannot act on GitHub for them. An access token is a credential.

socialIdentity.row.noTokenX.text: Homeroom stores no X access token for your account.
socialIdentity.row.noTokenX.description: Reassurance on the X row in Settings > Linked accounts. Homeroom only confirmed who the person is and cannot act on X for them. An access token is a credential.

socialIdentity.action.reconnect.description: Button on the GitHub or X row in Settings > Linked accounts. starts signing in at that provider again for an account that is linked but no longer counts.

socialIdentity.action.connect.description: Button on the GitHub or X row in Settings > Linked accounts. verb: starts signing in at that provider to connect the account to Homeroom.

socialIdentity.action.refreshHandle.description: Button on a connected GitHub or X row in Settings > Linked accounts. reads the account's current @name from the provider again, after it was renamed there.

socialIdentity.action.changeAccount.description: Button on a connected GitHub or X row in Settings > Linked accounts. verb: replaces the connected account with a different account at the same provider.

socialIdentity.row.strandedAttempt.text: Your last {{provider}} connection attempt didn't complete. Try Connect again. This can happen if the browser did not reach the sign-in page or the flow was cancelled. If {{provider}} reports a callback or redirect address error, ask an administrator to check its OAuth settings.

openrouter.catalog.refreshed_other.description: Status line in Settings > OpenRouter after the list of models was fetched again. {{count}} is how many models it holds.

openrouter.catalog.refreshFailed.description: Status line in Settings > OpenRouter when fetching the list of models again failed without a more specific message.

openrouter.favorite.failed.description: Status line in Settings > OpenRouter when starring or un-starring the selected model could not be saved.

openrouter.favorite.added.description: Status line in Settings > OpenRouter after the selected model was starred. {{model}} is the AI model's name.

openrouter.favorite.removed.description: Status line in Settings > OpenRouter after the star was taken off the selected model. {{model}} is the AI model's name.

openrouter.key.pasteFirst.text: Paste an OpenRouter API key first.
openrouter.key.pasteFirst.description: Status line in Settings > OpenRouter when the save button was pressed with the key field empty.

openrouter.key.verifying.description: Status line in Settings > OpenRouter while the pasted key is being checked. OpenRouter is a company name.

openrouter.key.saveFailed.description: Status line in Settings > OpenRouter when the pasted key could not be saved and the server gave no reason.

openrouter.key.saved.text: Saved, encrypted, and selected as your default coding agent.

openrouter.key.networkError.description: Status line in Settings > OpenRouter when saving the key did not reach the server. {{reason}} is the browser's own technical message.

openrouter.key.removeFailed.description: Status line in Settings > OpenRouter when the person's own OpenRouter key could not be removed.

openrouter.key.removed.description: Status line in Settings > OpenRouter after the person's own OpenRouter key was removed.

openrouter.key.removedDefaultReset.text: Key removed. Key removed; your default agent was reset to Claude Code.
openrouter.key.removedDefaultReset.description: Status line in Settings > OpenRouter after the person's own OpenRouter key was removed and, because of that, their default coding agent went back to Claude Code (a product name). The English says "Key removed" twice; once is enough in translation.

openrouter.default.chooseModelFirst.description: Status line in Settings > OpenRouter when "Save as my default coding agent" was pressed with no model selected.
