openrouter.default.saved.text: OpenRouter saved as your default session AI.
openrouter.default.saved.description: Status line in Settings > OpenRouter after OpenRouter, with the selected model, became what the person's coding sessions use by default.

openrouter.default.networkError.description: Status line in Settings > OpenRouter when making OpenRouter the default coding agent did not reach the server.

openrouter.claudeDefault.saveFailed.description: Status line in Settings > OpenRouter when making Claude Code the default coding agent could not be saved and the server gave no reason.

openrouter.claudeDefault.saved.text: Claude Code is now your default coding agent.
openrouter.claudeDefault.saved.description: Status line in Settings > OpenRouter after "Use Claude Code as my default instead" was pressed. Claude Code is a product name.

openrouter.claudeDefault.networkError.description: Status line in Settings > OpenRouter when making Claude Code the default coding agent did not reach the server.

password.status.tooShort.text: New password must be at least 8 characters.
password.status.tooShort.description: Status under the change-password form in Settings > Password when the new password is too short.

password.status.mismatch.description: Status under the change-password form in Settings > Password when the new password and its confirmation differ.

password.status.walletNativeOnly.text: Wallet signing is only available in the Homeroom app.
password.status.walletNativeOnly.description: Status under the change-password form in Settings > Password when creating a password by signing with the wallet was tried outside the Homeroom phone app.

password.status.verifyingIdentity.description: Status under the change-password form in Settings > Password while the wallet signature that proves who the person is gets checked.

password.status.noWalletAddress.text: Could not read your wallet address.
password.status.noWalletAddress.description: Status under the change-password form in Settings > Password when the phone app did not give the address of the person's wallet.

password.status.noChallenge.text: Could not get a challenge from the server.
password.status.noChallenge.description: Status under the change-password form in Settings > Password. A "challenge" is the one-time text the wallet must sign to prove who the person is; the server did not send one.

password.status.changeFailed.description: Status under the change-password form in Settings > Password when the server refused the change and gave no reason.

password.status.changed.description: Status under the change-password form in Settings > Password after the password was changed.

password.status.signatureDenied.description: Status under the change-password form in Settings > Password when the person declined to sign with their wallet.

password.status.walletChangeFailed.description: Status under the change-password form in Settings > Password when setting a password by wallet signature failed. "Wallet change" means the password change made with the wallet. {{reason}} is a technical message.

password.status.enterCurrent.description: Status under the change-password form in Settings > Password when the current password field is empty.

password.status.saving.description: Status under the change-password form in Settings > Password while the new password is being saved.

password.status.networkError.description: Status under the change-password form in Settings > Password when the request did not reach the server. {{reason}} is the browser's own technical message.

username.status.enterNew.description: Status under the change-username form in Settings > Username when the new username field is empty.

username.status.enterPassword.description: Status under the change-username form in Settings > Username when the password field, which confirms the change, is empty.

username.status.enterCode.text: Enter the six-digit code from the email.
username.status.enterCode.description: Status under the change-username form in Settings when the code field, which confirms the change for an account with no password, is empty.

username.status.sendingCode.description: Status under the change-username form in Settings while the code that confirms the change is being emailed.

username.status.codeSent.text: We sent a code to {{email}}. It expires in 10 minutes.
username.status.codeSent.description: Status under the change-username form in Settings after the confirmation code was emailed. {{email}} is the account's own verified address.

username.status.codeFailed.description: Status under the change-username form in Settings when emailing the confirmation code failed and the server gave no reason.

username.status.saving.description: Status under the change-username form in Settings > Username while the new username is being saved.

username.status.changeFailed.description: Status under the change-username form in Settings > Username when the server refused the change and gave no reason.

username.status.unchanged.description: Status under the change-username form in Settings > Username when the name entered is the one the person already has.

username.status.changed.description: Status under the change-username form in Settings > Username after the change. {{username}} is the new username; keep the @ before it.

username.status.networkError.description: Status under the change-username form in Settings > Username when the request did not reach the server. {{reason}} is the browser's own technical message.

signOut.failed.text: Could not sign out. Check your connection and try again.
signOut.failed.description: Error toast when pressing Sign out in Settings did not end the session.

apiKey.remove.confirmTitle.description: Title of the confirmation dialog before removing the saved Anthropic API key in Settings.

apiKey.remove.confirmMessage.text: Future chats will fall back to your weekly Homeroom credits.
apiKey.remove.confirmMessage.description: Body of the confirmation dialog before removing the saved Anthropic API key in Settings: AI usage will be paid from the platform's allowance again.

apiKey.remove.confirmButton.description: Red confirm button in the dialog that removes the saved Anthropic API key in Settings.

apiKey.remove.failed.description: Error under the Anthropic API key field in Settings when the saved key could not be removed and the server gave no reason.

apiKey.remove.done.description: Confirmation under the Anthropic API key field in Settings after the saved key was removed.

apiKey.remove.networkError.description: Error under the Anthropic API key field in Settings when removing the key did not reach the server. {{reason}} is the browser's own technical message.

grants.status.demoData.text: Demo data: changes are not saved.
grants.status.demoData.description: Status under the list of apps allowed to spend the person's AI allowance, in Settings > App AI permissions, when the rows are sample data on a preview server and a change was tried.

grants.status.networkError.description: Status under the list of apps allowed to spend the person's AI allowance, in Settings > App AI permissions when the request did not reach the server. {{reason}} is the browser's own technical message.

grants.status.invalidCap.description: Status under the list of apps allowed to spend the person's AI allowance, in Settings > App AI permissions, when the daily spending cap typed for an app is not a positive amount. "Cap" is a noun: an upper limit.

grants.status.capFailed.description: Status under the list of apps allowed to spend the person's AI allowance, in Settings > App AI permissions, when an app's new daily spending cap could not be saved and the server gave no reason.

grants.status.capUpdated.description: Status under the list of apps allowed to spend the person's AI allowance, in Settings > App AI permissions, after an app's daily spending cap was changed.

grants.status.spilloverFailed.description: Status under the list of apps allowed to spend the person's AI allowance, in Settings > App AI permissions, when the "spillover" switch (letting an app continue on the person's own API key once its cap is used up) could not be saved.

grants.status.spilloverEnabled.description: Status under the list of apps allowed to spend the person's AI allowance, in Settings > App AI permissions: the app may now continue on the person's own API key once its daily cap is used up.

grants.status.spilloverDisabled.description: Status under the list of apps allowed to spend the person's AI allowance, in Settings > App AI permissions: the app may no longer continue on the person's own API key once its daily cap is used up.

grants.revoke.confirmTitle.description: Title of the confirmation dialog before taking away an app's permission to use AI on the person's allowance, in Settings. {{app}} is the app's name; keep the quotation marks around it.

grants.revoke.confirmMessage.text: Its next AI call will fail immediately. The app can ask for access again later.
grants.revoke.confirmMessage.description: Body of the confirmation dialog before taking away an app's permission to use AI, in Settings. "Call" is a request to an AI model.

grants.revoke.confirmButton.description: Red confirm button in the dialog that takes away an app's permission to use AI on the person's allowance, in Settings.

grants.status.revokeFailed.description: Status under the list of apps allowed to spend the person's AI allowance, in Settings > App AI permissions, when an app's AI permission could not be taken away and the server gave no reason.

grants.status.revoked.description: Status under the list of apps allowed to spend the person's AI allowance, in Settings > App AI permissions, after an app's AI permission was taken away.

grants.status.reenableFailed.description: Status under the list of apps allowed to spend the person's AI allowance, in Settings > App AI permissions, when a revoked AI permission could not be given back and the server gave no reason.

grants.status.reenabledAtDefault.text: Re-enabled at the default {{cap}} daily cap.
grants.status.reenabledAtDefault.description: Status under the list of apps allowed to spend the person's AI allowance, in Settings > App AI permissions, after a revoked AI permission was given back with the standard daily spending cap because its old cap is no longer allowed. {{cap}} is a dollar amount such as $1.00.

grants.status.reenabled.description: Status under the list of apps allowed to spend the person's AI allowance, in Settings > App AI permissions, after a revoked AI permission was given back to the app.

notificationPrefs.status.demoData.text: Demo data: changes are not saved.
notificationPrefs.status.demoData.description: Status under the notification preferences (which kinds of app notifications the person receives) in Settings > Notifications, when the rows are sample data on a preview server and a change was tried.

notificationPrefs.status.networkError.description: Status under the notification preferences (which kinds of app notifications the person receives) in Settings > Notifications when the request did not reach the server. {{reason}} is the browser's own technical message.

notificationPrefs.status.saveFailed.description: Status under the notification preferences (which kinds of app notifications the person receives) in Settings > Notifications, when a changed default could not be saved and the server gave no reason.

notificationPrefs.status.saved.description: Status under the notification preferences (which kinds of app notifications the person receives) in Settings > Notifications, after a default was changed.

notificationPrefs.status.unknownApp.text: This app could not be identified.
notificationPrefs.status.unknownApp.description: Status under the notification preferences (which kinds of app notifications the person receives) in Settings > Notifications, when an app's own settings could not be reset because the app is not known.

notificationPrefs.status.resetFailed.description: Status under the notification preferences (which kinds of app notifications the person receives) in Settings > Notifications, when an app's own exceptions could not be removed and the server gave no reason.

notificationPrefs.status.reset.description: Status under the notification preferences (which kinds of app notifications the person receives) in Settings > Notifications, after an app's own exceptions were removed: the app now follows the account-wide defaults.

appPermissions.status.demoData.text: Demo data: changes are not saved.
appPermissions.status.demoData.description: Status under the list of device permissions granted to apps, in Settings > App device permissions, when the rows are sample data on a preview server and a change was tried.

appPermissions.status.networkError.description: Status under the list of device permissions granted to apps, in Settings > App device permissions when the request did not reach the server. {{reason}} is the browser's own technical message.

appPermissions.revoke.confirmTitle.description: Title of the confirmation dialog before taking away one device permission (camera, microphone, location…) from an app, in Settings.

appPermissions.revoke.confirmMessage.text: The app loses it the next time it opens. It can ask you again later.
appPermissions.revoke.confirmMessage.description: Body of the confirmation dialog before taking away a device permission from an app, in Settings. "It" is the permission, then the app.

appPermissions.revoke.confirmButton.description: Red confirm button in the dialog that takes away a device permission from an app, in Settings.

appPermissions.status.revokeFailed.description: Status under the list of device permissions granted to apps, in Settings > App device permissions, when a permission could not be taken away and the server gave no reason.

appPermissions.status.revoked.text: Revoked. It stops the next time the app opens.
appPermissions.status.revoked.description: Status under the list of device permissions granted to apps, in Settings > App device permissions, after a permission was taken away from an app. "It" is the app's use of the permission.

appPermissions.status.unknownApp.text: This app could not be identified.
appPermissions.status.unknownApp.description: Status under the list of device permissions granted to apps, in Settings > App device permissions, when a revoked permission could not be given back because the app is not known.

appPermissions.status.notDeclared.text: This app no longer asks for that permission.
appPermissions.status.notDeclared.description: Status under the list of device permissions granted to apps, in Settings > App device permissions, when a revoked permission could not be given back because the app has stopped requesting it.

appPermissions.status.reenableFailed.description: Status under the list of device permissions granted to apps, in Settings > App device permissions, when a revoked permission could not be given back and the server gave no reason.

appPermissions.status.reenabled.text: Re-enabled. It applies the next time the app opens.
appPermissions.status.reenabled.description: Status under the list of device permissions granted to apps, in Settings > App device permissions, after a revoked permission was given back to an app.

agentFiles.status.tooLarge.text: "{{file}}" is too large. The limit is 48 KB per file.
agentFiles.status.tooLarge.description: Status under the list of instruction files and skills for coding agents, in Settings > Agent instructions & skills, when the chosen file is too big to upload. {{file}} is the file's name; keep the quotation marks.

agentFiles.status.unreadable.description: Status under the list of instruction files and skills for coding agents, in Settings > Agent instructions & skills, when the browser could not read the chosen file.

agentFiles.form.titleSkill.description: Title of the small form shown after choosing a file to upload as a skill (a reusable procedure a coding agent can load), in Settings. {{file}} is the chosen file's name; keep the quotation marks.

agentFiles.form.titleInstruction.description: Title of the small form shown after choosing a file to upload as an instruction file (standing guidance a coding agent always reads), in Settings. {{file}} is the chosen file's name; keep the quotation marks.

agentFiles.status.demoData.text: Demo data: changes are not saved.
agentFiles.status.demoData.description: Status under the list of instruction files and skills for coding agents, in Settings > Agent instructions & skills, when the rows are sample data on a preview server and a change was tried.

agentFiles.status.nameRequired.description: Status under the list of instruction files and skills for coding agents, in Settings > Agent instructions & skills, when the name field of the upload form is empty.

agentFiles.status.saveFailed.description: Status under the list of instruction files and skills for coding agents, in Settings > Agent instructions & skills, when the upload could not be saved and the server gave no reason.

agentFiles.status.saved.text: Saved "{{name}}". It applies from your next run.
agentFiles.status.saved.description: Status under the list of instruction files and skills for coding agents, in Settings > Agent instructions & skills, after a file was uploaded. {{name}} is the name it was saved under; keep the quotation marks. A "run" is one job the coding agent does.

agentFiles.status.networkError.description: Status under the list of instruction files and skills for coding agents, in Settings > Agent instructions & skills when the request did not reach the server. {{reason}} is the browser's own technical message.

agentFiles.delete.confirmTitle.description: Title of the confirmation dialog before deleting an instruction file or skill in Settings. {{name}} is the file's name; keep the quotation marks.

agentFiles.delete.confirmMessage.text: The coding agent stops using it from your next run. This cannot be undone.
agentFiles.delete.confirmMessage.description: Body of the confirmation dialog before deleting an instruction file or skill in Settings. A "run" is one job the coding agent does.

agentFiles.delete.confirmButton.description: Red confirm button in the dialog that deletes an instruction file or skill for coding agents, in Settings.

agentFiles.status.deleteFailed.description: Status under the list of instruction files and skills for coding agents, in Settings > Agent instructions & skills, when a file could not be deleted and the server gave no reason.

agentFiles.status.deleted.description: Status under the list of instruction files and skills for coding agents, in Settings > Agent instructions & skills, after a file was deleted. {{name}} is the file's name; keep the quotation marks.

wallet.status.startFailed.description: Status in Settings > Homeroom Wallet when linking a crypto wallet to the account could not be started and the server gave no reason.

wallet.status.networkError.description: Status in Settings > Homeroom Wallet when the request did not reach the server. {{reason}} is the browser's own technical message.

wallet.status.linked.description: Status in Settings > Homeroom Wallet after the wallet app scanned the QR code and the wallet was linked to the account.

wallet.status.qrExpired.description: Status in Settings > Homeroom Wallet when the QR code for linking a wallet was not scanned in time.

wallet.link.expiresIn.description: Countdown under the QR code for linking a wallet in Settings > Homeroom Wallet. {{time}} is minutes and seconds, such as 4:59.

wallet.unlink.confirmTitle.description: Title of the confirmation dialog before removing the link between the account and its crypto wallet, in Settings. Homeroom is the product name.

wallet.unlink.confirmButton.description: Red confirm button in the dialog that removes the link between the account and its crypto wallet, in Settings. A verb.

wallet.status.unlinkFailed.description: Status in Settings > Homeroom Wallet when the wallet could not be unlinked and the server gave no reason.

wallet.status.unlinked.description: Status in Settings > Homeroom Wallet after the wallet was unlinked from the account.

usernode.readError.timeout.text: The Homeroom app didn’t respond in time. It may still be starting up.
usernode.readError.timeout.description: Reason shown in Settings > Homeroom app when the phone app's settings could not be read: the app did not answer in time.

usernode.readError.rejected.text: The Homeroom app reported an error.
usernode.readError.rejected.description: Reason shown in Settings > Homeroom app when the phone app's settings could not be read: the app answered with an error.

usernode.readError.probeInconclusive.text: The Homeroom app hasn’t re-established its secure connection for settings. Reopening the app usually fixes this.
usernode.readError.probeInconclusive.description: Reason shown in Settings > Homeroom app when the phone app's settings could not be read: the secure connection between this screen and the app is not confirmed yet.

usernode.readError.noTransport.text: This screen can’t reach the Homeroom app from here.
usernode.readError.noTransport.description: Reason shown in Settings > Homeroom app when the phone app's settings could not be read: there is no channel from this screen to the app.

usernode.readError.notNative.text: This screen can’t reach the Homeroom app from here.
usernode.readError.notNative.description: Reason shown in Settings > Homeroom app when the phone app's settings could not be read: this screen is not running inside the phone app.

usernode.readError.pageChanged.text: The request was cancelled because this page changed.
usernode.readError.pageChanged.description: Reason shown in Settings > Homeroom app when the phone app's settings could not be read: the person moved to another page before the app answered.

usernode.readError.privilegedUnavailable.text: The Homeroom app refused this screen’s secure connection. See “Homeroom app: connection” below.
usernode.readError.privilegedUnavailable.description: Reason shown in Settings > Homeroom app when the phone app's settings could not be read: the app refused the secure connection. “Homeroom app: connection” is the title of the panel below; translate it the same way there.

usernode.readError.fallback.text: The Homeroom app returned no settings.
usernode.readError.fallback.description: Reason shown in Settings > Homeroom app when the phone app's settings could not be read: no more specific cause is known.

usernode.connection.state.ready.description: Short state label on the "Homeroom app: connection" panel in Settings > Homeroom app, describing the secure connection between this screen and the phone app: it is up.

usernode.connection.state.blockedFrame.description: Short state label on the "Homeroom app: connection" panel in Settings > Homeroom app, describing the secure connection between this screen and the phone app: the app refused it.

usernode.connection.state.unsupported.description: Short state label on the "Homeroom app: connection" panel in Settings > Homeroom app, describing the secure connection between this screen and the phone app: this version of the app is too old to have it. "Build" is a noun: a version of the app.

usernode.connection.state.inconclusive.description: Short state label on the "Homeroom app: connection" panel in Settings > Homeroom app, describing the secure connection between this screen and the phone app: the app has not answered yet.

usernode.connection.state.unattached.description: Short state label on the "Homeroom app: connection" panel in Settings > Homeroom app, describing the secure connection between this screen and the phone app: the app never answered the request.

usernode.connection.state.unknown.description: Short state label on the "Homeroom app: connection" panel in Settings > Homeroom app, describing the secure connection between this screen and the phone app: this screen has not asked for it so far.

usernode.connection.reason.ready.text: This screen can manage the app’s settings.
usernode.connection.reason.ready.description: Explanation on the "Homeroom app: connection" panel in Settings > Homeroom app: the secure connection is up.

usernode.connection.reason.blockedFrame.text: The app is refusing this screen’s secure connection, so app settings and app sign-out can’t be changed from here. Force-close the app and reopen it, which usually re-establishes it. If it keeps happening, reinstalling the app clears the stuck state.
usernode.connection.reason.blockedFrame.description: Explanation on the "Homeroom app: connection" panel in Settings > Homeroom app: the app refuses the connection, with what to try.

usernode.connection.reason.unsupported.text: This app build predates the secure connection this screen uses. Update the Homeroom app to manage its settings here.
usernode.connection.reason.unsupported.description: Explanation on the "Homeroom app: connection" panel in Settings > Homeroom app: the installed version of the app is too old. "Build" is a noun: a version of the app.

usernode.connection.reason.inconclusive.text: The app hasn’t answered yet, so we can’t tell whether the secure connection is up. It may still be starting, so try again in a moment.
usernode.connection.reason.inconclusive.description: Explanation on the "Homeroom app: connection" panel in Settings > Homeroom app: the app has not answered yet.

usernode.connection.reason.unattached.text: The app never answered this screen’s secure connection request. Force-close the app and reopen it; if that doesn’t help, reinstalling the app clears the stuck state.
usernode.connection.reason.unattached.description: Explanation on the "Homeroom app: connection" panel in Settings > Homeroom app: the app never answered, with what to try.

usernode.connection.reason.unknown.text: This screen hasn’t needed the app’s secure connection yet.
usernode.connection.reason.unknown.description: Explanation on the "Homeroom app: connection" panel in Settings > Homeroom app: nothing has asked for the connection so far, so its state is not known.

usernode.action.notAccepting.text: The Homeroom app isn’t accepting changes from this screen. Force-close and reopen the app, then try again.
usernode.action.notAccepting.description: Toast or notice in Settings > Homeroom app when the phone app refuses an action from this screen because their secure connection is down.

usernode.notif.openingPermissionPrompt.description: Notice under the notification permission row in Settings > Homeroom app (inside the phone app), on Android, right after the row was tapped: the system dialog asking for permission is about to appear.

usernode.notif.openingNotificationPrompt.description: Notice under the notification permission row in Settings > Homeroom app (inside the phone app), on iPhone, right after the row was tapped: the system dialog asking to allow notifications is about to appear.

usernode.notif.preview.text: This is a preview of the in-app row. The notification permission itself lives in the Homeroom app.
usernode.notif.preview.description: Notice under the notification permission row in Settings > Homeroom app (inside the phone app), when the row is shown in a browser as a preview and tapping it cannot ask for anything.

usernode.notif.onlyInApp.text: Notification permission is only available inside the Homeroom app.
usernode.notif.onlyInApp.description: Notice under the notification permission row in Settings > Homeroom app (inside the phone app), when this screen is not running inside the phone app.

usernode.notif.alreadyAllowed.text: Notifications are already allowed for Homeroom.
usernode.notif.alreadyAllowed.description: Notice under the notification permission row in Settings > Homeroom app (inside the phone app), when the row was tapped and the permission is already granted.

usernode.notif.noAnswer.text: The Homeroom app didn’t respond to the permission request. Force-close and reopen the app, then try again.
usernode.notif.noAnswer.description: Notice under the notification permission row in Settings > Homeroom app (inside the phone app), when the phone app did not answer within 20 seconds.

usernode.notif.requestFailed.text: The permission request could not be started.
usernode.notif.requestFailed.description: Notice under the notification permission row in Settings > Homeroom app (inside the phone app), when asking the phone app for the permission failed.

usernode.notif.permissionGranted.description: Notice under the notification permission row in Settings > Homeroom app (inside the phone app), on Android, after the person granted the permission.

usernode.notif.nowAllowed.text: Notifications are now allowed for Homeroom.
usernode.notif.nowAllowed.description: Notice under the notification permission row in Settings > Homeroom app (inside the phone app), on iPhone, after the person allowed notifications.

usernode.notif.unsupported.text: This version of the Homeroom app can’t open the notification prompt. Update the app from the App Store.
usernode.notif.unsupported.description: Notice under the notification permission row in Settings > Homeroom app (inside the phone app), when the installed app is too old to ask for the permission. App Store is Apple's store name.

usernode.notif.deniedAndroid.text: Permission was denied. Allow notifications in the system settings for Homeroom.
usernode.notif.deniedAndroid.description: Notice under the notification permission row in Settings > Homeroom app (inside the phone app), on Android, when the permission was denied and can only be changed in the phone's settings.

usernode.notif.deniedIos.text: Notifications are turned off for Homeroom. iOS only shows its prompt once, so this has to be changed in Settings › Notifications › Homeroom.
usernode.notif.deniedIos.description: Notice under the notification permission row in Settings > Homeroom app (inside the phone app), on iPhone, when notifications were denied. "Settings › Notifications › Homeroom" is the path in the iPhone's own Settings app; use the names iOS shows in your language.

usernode.notif.declined.description: Notice under the notification permission row in Settings > Homeroom app (inside the phone app), when the person dismissed the system dialog without granting the permission.

usernode.notif.silent.text: The Homeroom app closed without showing the notification prompt. Reopen the app and try again, or allow notifications in Settings › Notifications › Homeroom.
usernode.notif.silent.description: Notice under the notification permission row in Settings > Homeroom app (inside the phone app), when the system dialog never appeared. "Settings › Notifications › Homeroom" is the path in the iPhone's own Settings app; use the names iOS shows in your language.

usernode.notif.couldNotOpen.text: The notification prompt could not be opened.
usernode.notif.couldNotOpen.description: Notice under the notification permission row in Settings > Homeroom app (inside the phone app), when the system dialog could not be shown and no more specific reason is known.

terms.noneToReview.text: No terms to review right now
terms.noneToReview.description: Toast when the person asked to see the platform's terms and none are published.

terms.loadFailed.description: Error toast when the platform's terms could not be fetched.

terms.fallbackTitle.description: Title of the sheet that shows the platform's terms and asks the person to accept them, when the terms document has no title of its own. Noun: the terms of use.

terms.firstRunIntro.text: Reviewing the terms is part of joining the platform. Please read the full terms, then choose whether to accept.
terms.firstRunIntro.description: Introduction at the top of the sheet that shows the platform's terms and asks the person to accept them, when it opens by itself the first time a person arrives.

terms.version.description: Small line in the sheet that shows the platform's terms and asks the person to accept them: which version of the terms this is. {{version}} is a version label such as 3 or 2025-01.

terms.published.description: Small line in the sheet that shows the platform's terms and asks the person to accept them, after the version: when this version was published. {{date}} is a date. Lower case because it follows "Version 3 ·".

terms.readFull.description: Link in the sheet that shows the platform's terms and asks the person to accept them: opens the complete terms document in a new tab.

terms.acceptedOn.description: Status in the sheet that shows the platform's terms and asks the person to accept them when the person has already accepted this version. {{date}} is the date they accepted.

terms.accepted.description: Status in the sheet that shows the platform's terms and asks the person to accept them when the person has already accepted this version and the date is not known.

terms.notAccepted.text: You have not accepted this version yet.
terms.notAccepted.description: Status in the sheet that shows the platform's terms and asks the person to accept them when the person has not accepted this version.

terms.consentFailed.description: Error toast when the person's answer (accept or decline) to the platform's terms could not be saved.

terms.accept.description: Main button in the sheet that shows the platform's terms and asks the person to accept them: records that the person accepts them.

terms.acceptedToast.description: Toast after the person accepted the platform's terms.

terms.decline.description: Second button in the sheet that shows the platform's terms and asks the person to accept them, shown the first time: records that the person does not accept the terms for now.

terms.declinedToast.text: You can accept the terms later from your profile
terms.declinedToast.description: Toast after the person declined the platform's terms: their Profile screen keeps a way to accept them later.

usernode.privacy.strictFacematch.description: Switch in the "privacy & identity" block of Settings > Homeroom app: require a stricter match between the person's face and their passport photo during identity verification.

usernode.privacy.openZkIdentity.description: Button in the "privacy & identity" block of Settings > Homeroom app: opens the phone app's identity verification screen. "Open" is a verb; ZK (zero-knowledge) stays as it is.

usernode.privacy.restartZkChallenge.description: Red button in the "privacy & identity" block of Settings > Homeroom app: throws away the identity verification in progress so it can be started again. ZK (zero-knowledge) stays as it is.

usernode.diagnostics.debugMode.description: Switch in the diagnostics block of Settings > Homeroom app: turns on extra logging in the phone app.

usernode.diagnostics.deviceBenchmark.description: Button in the diagnostics block of Settings > Homeroom app: opens the phone app's screen that measures the device's speed.

usernode.diagnostics.httpLogs.description: Button in the diagnostics block of Settings > Homeroom app: opens the phone app's screen listing its network requests.

usernode.about.reviewTerms.description: Button in the "about & legal" block of Settings > Homeroom app, when the person has not accepted the current terms: opens them.

usernode.about.terms.description: Button in the "about & legal" block of Settings > Homeroom app: opens the platform's terms of use.

usernode.about.privacy.description: Button in the "about & legal" block of Settings > Homeroom app, beside Terms: opens Homeroom's privacy notice, which says what personal data Homeroom collects and how it uses it, in the phone's browser.

usernode.about.appVersionBuild.description: Part of the version line in the "about & legal" block of Settings > Homeroom app: the phone app's version and build number.

usernode.about.appVersion.description: Part of the version line in the "about & legal" block of Settings > Homeroom app: the phone app's version.

usernode.about.nodeVersion.description: Part of the version line in the "about & legal" block of Settings > Homeroom app: the version of the network node software inside the phone app. "Node" is that software, not Node.js.

usernode.connection.appVersionBuild.description: Part of the small version line on the "Homeroom app: connection" panel in Settings: the phone app's version and build number.

usernode.connection.appVersion.description: Part of the small version line on the "Homeroom app: connection" panel in Settings: the phone app's version.

usernode.connection.bridgeVersion.description: Part of the small version line on the "Homeroom app: connection" panel in Settings: the version number of the bridge, the channel between this screen and the phone app. "v" abbreviates version.

usernode.connection.rowLabel.description: Label of the status row on the "Homeroom app: connection" panel in Settings: the secure channel between this screen and the phone app.

usernode.connection.state.unavailable.description: Short state label on the "Homeroom app: connection" panel in Settings when the connection's state is one Homeroom does not recognise.

usernode.connection.connectWallet.description: Button on the "Homeroom app: connection" panel in Settings: opens a dialog to attach a wallet the person already has, when the app could not give them a new one.

usernode.permissions.heading.description: Heading of the device permissions block in Settings > Homeroom app. Homeroom is the product name.

usernode.permissions.descriptionAndroid.text: Block production needs the app to wake your device at exact slot times.
usernode.permissions.descriptionAndroid.description: Explanation under the device permissions heading in Settings > Homeroom app, on Android. Block production is the phone taking its turn ("slot") to produce a block for the network.

usernode.permissions.descriptionIos.text: Notifications let Homeroom alert you about node and account activity.
usernode.permissions.descriptionIos.description: Explanation under the device permissions heading in Settings > Homeroom app, on iPhone. "Node" is the network node running in the phone app.

usernode.permissions.exactAlarms.description: Label of the permission row in Settings > Homeroom app on Android: the system permission to schedule alarms at exact times.

usernode.permissions.notifications.description: Label of the permission row in Settings > Homeroom app on iPhone: the system permission to show notifications.

usernode.permissions.granted.description: State shown on the permission row in Settings > Homeroom app: the system permission has been granted.

usernode.permissions.notGranted.description: State shown on the permission row in Settings > Homeroom app: the system permission has not been granted.

usernode.permissions.exactAlarmsActionNa.description: Accessible name of the tappable permission row in Settings > Homeroom app on Android: the row's label, then what tapping it does.

usernode.permissions.notificationsAction.description: Accessible name of the tappable permission row in Settings > Homeroom app on iPhone: the row's label, then what tapping it does.

usernode.permissions.requestPermissions.description: Button under the permission row in Settings > Homeroom app on Android: opens the system dialog that asks for the permission. "Request" is a verb.

usernode.permissions.allowNotifications.description: Button under the permission row in Settings > Homeroom app on iPhone: opens the system dialog that asks to allow notifications.

usernode.permissions.batteryOptimization.description: Label of a status row in Settings > Homeroom app on Android: whether the system restricts the app in the background to save battery.

usernode.permissions.batteryUnrestricted.description: State on the Battery optimization row in Settings > Homeroom app: the system does not restrict the app in the background (the good state).

usernode.permissions.batteryRestricted.description: State on the Battery optimization row in Settings > Homeroom app: the system restricts the app in the background.

usernode.permissions.openBatterySettings.description: Button in Settings > Homeroom app on Android: opens the phone's battery settings for the app. "Open" is a verb.

usernode.permissions.device.description: Small line in the device permissions block of Settings > Homeroom app on Android. {{manufacturer}} is the phone maker's name, such as Samsung.

usernode.socialPush.stuck.text: The Homeroom app isn’t accepting this screen’s secure connection, so notifications can’t be set up. See “Homeroom app: connection” above.
usernode.socialPush.stuck.description: Reason in the activity notifications block of Settings > Homeroom app when the phone app refuses the secure connection. “Homeroom app: connection” is the title of the panel above; translate it the same way there.

usernode.socialPush.finishingSignIn.text: Finishing secure app sign-in before enabling notifications…
usernode.socialPush.finishingSignIn.description: Reason in the activity notifications block of Settings > Homeroom app while the phone app is still signing in and notifications cannot be set up yet.

usernode.socialPush.unavailable.description: Reason in the activity notifications block of Settings > Homeroom app when the notification state could not be read.

usernode.socialPush.statusOff.description: Status under the "Activity notifications" switch in Settings > Homeroom app: push notifications are off on this phone.

usernode.socialPush.statusOn.text: On. This device is registered for activity notifications.
usernode.socialPush.statusOn.description: Status under the "Activity notifications" switch in Settings > Homeroom app: push notifications are on and this phone is set up to receive them.

usernode.socialPush.statusDenied.text: Notification permission is denied in the device settings.
usernode.socialPush.statusDenied.description: Status under the "Activity notifications" switch in Settings > Homeroom app: the phone's own settings block notifications for the app.

usernode.socialPush.statusEnabling.description: Status under the "Activity notifications" switch in Settings > Homeroom app while the phone is being registered for push notifications.

usernode.socialPush.statusNotActive.text: Enabled, but delivery is not active yet.
usernode.socialPush.statusNotActive.description: Status under the "Activity notifications" switch in Settings > Homeroom app: the switch is on but the phone is not yet registered to receive push notifications.

usernode.blockProduction.checkFailed.text: Could not check block-production status right now.
usernode.blockProduction.checkFailed.description: Note in the block production block of Settings > Homeroom app when the status could not be fetched.

usernode.blockProduction.released.text: Released. Your node produces blocks when it wins slots.
usernode.blockProduction.released.description: Note in the block production block of Settings > Homeroom app: an administrator has released the person's keys, so their phone now produces blocks when its turn ("slot") comes.

usernode.blockProduction.pending.text: Request pending. You’ll start producing automatically once an admin releases your keys.
usernode.blockProduction.pending.description: Note in the block production block of Settings > Homeroom app: the person has asked to produce blocks and waits for an administrator. "Request" is a noun.

usernode.blockProduction.needsAccess.text: Available once your account has platform access.
usernode.blockProduction.needsAccess.description: Note in the block production block of Settings > Homeroom app: asking to produce blocks is possible only after the account has been let in to the platform.

usernode.blockProduction.requestFailed.description: Error toast in Settings > Homeroom app when asking to produce blocks failed and the server gave no reason. "Request" is a noun.

usernode.blockProduction.requestSent.text: Request sent. An admin will release your keys
usernode.blockProduction.requestSent.description: Toast in Settings > Homeroom app after the person asked to produce blocks. "Request" is a noun.

usernode.widgetIcons.sending.label.description: Label of a status row in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: what kind of icon Homeroom is sending to the widget now.

usernode.widgetIcons.sending.pair.description: Value of the "Sending" row in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: each icon is sent in a light and a dark version.

usernode.widgetIcons.sending.undecided.description: Value of the "Sending" row in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: it is not yet known whether the widget can store two versions, so one version ("face") is sent for now.

usernode.widgetIcons.sending.singleDark.description: Value of the "Sending" row in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: only one version ("face") of each icon is sent, the dark one.

usernode.widgetIcons.sending.singleLight.description: Value of the "Sending" row in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: only one version ("face") of each icon is sent, the light one.

usernode.widgetIcons.sending.singleOther.description: Value of the "Sending" row in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: only one version ("face") of each icon is sent. {{scheme}} is a technical name for which one, shown as it is; a fallback for a value other than light or dark.

usernode.widgetIcons.verdictBound.description: Note in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: the conclusion about what the widget can store was reached for this version of the phone app. {{version}} is the app version and {{build}} its build number, or "?" when unknown.

usernode.widgetIcons.verdictUnbound.text: Verdict bound to app version: unknown, the verdict is re-confirmed each time
usernode.widgetIcons.verdictUnbound.description: Note in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: the phone app's version is not known, so the conclusion about what the widget can store is checked again on every load.

usernode.widgetIcons.readError.description: Warning note in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget when a read from the phone app failed. {{method}} is the technical name of the call that failed; {{reason}} is a complete sentence saying why.

usernode.widgetIcons.mechanism.label.description: Label of a status row in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: whether this phone pins app shortcuts through the home-screen widget.

usernode.widgetIcons.mechanism.available.description: Value of the "Widget shortcuts" row in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: this phone uses the widget for shortcuts.

usernode.widgetIcons.mechanism.otherDevi.description: Value of the "Widget shortcuts" row in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: this phone pins shortcuts another way. {{mechanism}} is the technical name of that way, shown as it is.

usernode.widgetIcons.mechanism.unavailab.description: Value of the "Widget shortcuts" row in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: this phone cannot pin shortcuts at all.

usernode.widgetIcons.registry.label.description: Label of a status row in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: the widget's own list of pinned shortcuts.

usernode.widgetIcons.registry.loaded_one.description: Value of the "Pinned registry" row in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: the list was read. {{count}} is how many shortcuts are pinned.

usernode.widgetIcons.registry.loaded_oth.description: Value of the "Pinned registry" row in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: the list was read. {{count}} is how many shortcuts are pinned.

usernode.widgetIcons.registry.unreadable.description: Value of the "Pinned registry" row in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: the widget's list of pinned shortcuts could not be read.

usernode.widgetIcons.capability.label.description: Label of a status row in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: whether the phone app says it supports a separate dark version of icons.

usernode.widgetIcons.capability.advertis.description: Value of the "Dark icon capability" row in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: the phone app says it supports dark icons.

usernode.widgetIcons.capability.notAdver.description: Value of the "Dark icon capability" row in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: the phone app does not list support for dark icons.

usernode.widgetIcons.capability.unknown.description: Value of the "Dark icon capability" row in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: the phone app did not answer whether it supports dark icons.

usernode.widgetIcons.verdict.label.description: Label of a status row in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: what the widget itself was observed to store.

usernode.widgetIcons.verdict.supported.description: Value of the "Confirmed by the widget" row in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: the widget keeps both the light and the dark version ("faces") of an icon.

usernode.widgetIcons.verdict.unsupported.description: Value of the "Confirmed by the widget" row in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: the widget keeps only one version ("face") of an icon.

usernode.widgetIcons.verdict.unconfirmed.description: Value of the "Confirmed by the widget" row in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: it has not been observed yet what the widget stores.

usernode.widgetIcons.lastCheck.at.description: Note in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: when the last pass that refreshes the widget's icons ran, and what it did. The pass ran and left no outcome. {{when}} is a date and time.

usernode.widgetIcons.lastCheck.never.description: Note in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: when the last pass that refreshes the widget's icons ran, and what it did. No pass has run.

usernode.widgetIcons.lastCheck.atSkipped.text: Last icon check: {{when}}: skipped, not the widget mechanism
usernode.widgetIcons.lastCheck.atSkipped.description: Note in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: when the last pass that refreshes the widget's icons ran, and what it did. The latest pass did not run because this device does not use the widget. {{when}} is the date and time of the last pass that did run.

usernode.widgetIcons.lastCheck.neverSkip.text: Last icon check: never: skipped, not the widget mechanism
usernode.widgetIcons.lastCheck.neverSkip.description: Note in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: when the last pass that refreshes the widget's icons ran, and what it did. No pass has run, and the latest one was skipped because this device does not use the widget.

usernode.widgetIcons.lastCheck.atSkipped.text: Last icon check: {{when}}: skipped, no shortcut bridge
usernode.widgetIcons.lastCheck.atSkipped.description: Note in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: when the last pass that refreshes the widget's icons ran, and what it did. The latest pass did not run because the app cannot talk to the phone's shortcut feature. {{when}} is the date and time of the last pass that did run.

usernode.widgetIcons.lastCheck.neverSkip.text: Last icon check: never: skipped, no shortcut bridge
usernode.widgetIcons.lastCheck.neverSkip.description: Note in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: when the last pass that refreshes the widget's icons ran, and what it did. No pass has run, and the latest one was skipped because the app cannot talk to the phone's shortcut feature.

usernode.widgetIcons.lastCheck.atNothing.text: Last icon check: {{when}}: nothing to send
usernode.widgetIcons.lastCheck.atNothing.description: Note in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: when the last pass that refreshes the widget's icons ran, and what it did. The pass found every icon up to date. {{when}} is a date and time.

usernode.widgetIcons.lastCheck.neverNoth.text: Last icon check: never: nothing to send
usernode.widgetIcons.lastCheck.neverNoth.description: Note in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: when the last pass that refreshes the widget's icons ran, and what it did. Shown when no time was recorded although a pass found every icon up to date.

usernode.widgetIcons.lastCheck.atSent_on.description: Note in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: when the last pass that refreshes the widget's icons ran, and what it did. The pass sent {{count}} icons to the widget. {{when}} is a date and time.

usernode.widgetIcons.lastCheck.atSent_ot.description: Note in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: when the last pass that refreshes the widget's icons ran, and what it did. The pass sent {{count}} icons to the widget. {{when}} is a date and time.

usernode.widgetIcons.lastCheck.neverSent.description: Note in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: when the last pass that refreshes the widget's icons ran, and what it did. Shown when no time was recorded although a pass sent {{count}} icons to the widget.

Note in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: when the last pass that refreshes the widget's icons ran, and what it did. Shown when no time was recorded although a pass sent {{count}} icons to the widget.

usernode.widgetIcons.lastCheck.atSentRef.description: Note in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: when the last pass that refreshes the widget's icons ran, and what it did. The pass sent {{count}} icons and the phone refused {{refused}} more. {{when}} is a date and time.

Note in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: when the last pass that refreshes the widget's icons ran, and what it did. The pass sent {{count}} icons and the phone refused {{refused}} more. {{when}} is a date and time.

usernode.widgetIcons.lastCheck.neverSent.text: Last icon check: never: sent {{count}}, {{refused}} refused
usernode.widgetIcons.lastCheck.neverSent.description: Note in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: when the last pass that refreshes the widget's icons ran, and what it did. Shown when no time was recorded although a pass sent {{count}} icons and the phone refused {{refused}} more.

usernode.widgetIcons.lastCheck.neverSent.text: Last icon check: never: sent {{count}}, {{refused}} refused
usernode.widgetIcons.lastCheck.neverSent.description: Note in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: when the last pass that refreshes the widget's icons ran, and what it did. Shown when no time was recorded although a pass sent {{count}} icons and the phone refused {{refused}} more.

usernode.widgetIcons.entry.none.text: No shortcuts are pinned to the widget.
usernode.widgetIcons.entry.none.description: Shown in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget in place of the list of pinned shortcuts when there are none.

usernode.widgetIcons.entry.foreign.description: Line under a pinned shortcut in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: the shortcut was not pinned by Homeroom. Lower case: a short technical note.

usernode.widgetIcons.entry.appNotLoaded.description: Line under a pinned shortcut in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: Homeroom has not loaded the app this shortcut opens, so it cannot check its icon. Lower case: a short technical note.

usernode.widgetIcons.entry.iconYes.description: Fact in the line under a pinned shortcut in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: the widget holds an icon for it. Lower case, terse.

usernode.widgetIcons.entry.iconNo.description: Fact in the line under a pinned shortcut in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: the widget holds no icon for it. Lower case, terse.

usernode.widgetIcons.entry.iconUnknown.description: Fact in the line under a pinned shortcut in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: it is not known whether the widget holds an icon for it. Keep the dash.

usernode.widgetIcons.entry.darkYes.description: Fact in the line under a pinned shortcut in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: the widget holds a dark version of its icon. Lower case, terse.

usernode.widgetIcons.entry.darkNo.description: Fact in the line under a pinned shortcut in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: the widget holds no dark version of its icon. Lower case, terse.

usernode.widgetIcons.entry.darkUnknown.description: Fact in the line under a pinned shortcut in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: it is not known whether the widget holds a dark version of its icon. Keep the dash.

usernode.widgetIcons.entry.sentCurrent.description: Fact in the line under a pinned shortcut in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: the icon the widget holds is the one Homeroom last sent. Lower case, terse.

usernode.widgetIcons.entry.sentStale.description: Fact in the line under a pinned shortcut in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" diagnostics box in Settings, which reports how app icons were sent to the phone's home-screen widget: the icon the widget holds is older than the one Homeroom wants there. Lower case, terse.

usernode.connection.diagnosticsCopied.description: Toast after "Copy diagnostics" on the "Homeroom app: connection" panel in Settings copied the technical report to the clipboard.

usernode.connection.diagnosticsCopyFaile.description: Error toast when "Copy diagnostics" on the "Homeroom app: connection" panel in Settings could not copy the technical report.

usernode.privacy.openZkIdentityFailed.description: Error toast in Settings > Homeroom app when the phone app's identity verification screen could not be opened. ZK stays as it is.

usernode.diagnostics.openBenchmarkFailed.description: Error toast in Settings > Homeroom app when the phone app's device speed test screen could not be opened.

usernode.diagnostics.openLogsFailed.description: Error toast in Settings > Homeroom app when the phone app's network log screen could not be opened.

usernode.privacy.restart.confirmTitle.description: Title of the confirmation dialog before throwing away an identity verification in progress, in Settings > Homeroom app. ZK (zero-knowledge) stays as it is.

usernode.privacy.restart.confirmMessage.text: Your in-progress identity registration will be discarded.
usernode.privacy.restart.confirmMessage.description: Body of the confirmation dialog before restarting identity verification in Settings > Homeroom app.

usernode.privacy.restart.confirmButton.description: Red confirm button in the dialog that throws away an identity verification in progress so it can start again, in Settings > Homeroom app.

usernode.privacy.restart.done.description: Toast in Settings > Homeroom app after the identity verification in progress was thrown away. "Reset" is a past participle: the state has been reset.

list.dot.description: Joins two short independent facts on one line in Settings, for example "Free · verified" in the OpenRouter model list or "App 1.4 · Bridge v5". {{first}} and {{second}} are each already a complete translated phrase. Use the separator your language uses between such facts.

password.status.set.text: Password set. You can now sign in with it.
password.status.set.description: Status under the password form in Settings > Password after an account that signed in only with an email code set its first password.
